## Keys

Key commands work on keys regardless of the type of value they hold. This page lists every key command on the `Redis` service, grouped by purpose, with the option types they take.

### Inspecting Keys

These commands check whether keys exist and what they hold:

| Command         | Result       | Description                                              |
| --------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#exists`  | `Long`       | Counts how many of the given keys exist                  |
| `Redis#typeOf`  | `RedisType`  | Returns the type of the value stored at a key            |
| `Redis#randomKey` | `Option[A]` | Returns a random key, or `None` when the database is empty |
| `Redis#touch`   | `Long`       | Updates the last access time of the given keys           |

`Redis#exists` counts a key once for every time it is listed, so `exists("a", "a")` returns `2` when `a` exists. `Redis#typeOf` returns a `RedisType`, which has the cases `String`, `List`, `Set`, `SortedSet`, `Hash` and `Stream`. To check a key and branch on its type:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def describe(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, String] =
  redis.typeOf("user:1").map {
    case RedisType.Hash => "a hash"
    case other          => s"something else: $other"
  }
```

`Redis#randomKey` needs a result type like any command that returns a key. To pick any key:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def anyKey(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  redis.randomKey.returning[String]
```

### Deleting Keys

Both commands take one key and any number of extra keys, and return how many were removed:

| Command        | Result | Description                                                    |
| -------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#del`    | `Long` | Removes the keys and frees their memory immediately            |
| `Redis#unlink` | `Long` | Removes the keys and frees their memory in a background thread |

`Redis#unlink` is the better choice for large values because it does not block the server. To delete several keys:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def cleanup(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.unlink("cache:a", "cache:b", "cache:c")
```

`Redis#flushall` deletes every key in every database. Its `sync` parameter defaults to `false`, which sends `ASYNC`, and `true` sends `SYNC`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def reset(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Unit] =
  redis.flushall(sync = true)
```

### Expiration

Expiry commands set, read and clear the time to live of a key:

| Command            | Result     | Description                                         |
| ------------------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#expire`     | `Boolean`  | Expires the key after a `Duration`, in seconds      |
| `Redis#pExpire`    | `Boolean`  | Expires the key after a `Duration`, in milliseconds |
| `Redis#expireAt`   | `Boolean`  | Expires the key at an `Instant`, in seconds         |
| `Redis#pExpireAt`  | `Boolean`  | Expires the key at an `Instant`, in milliseconds    |
| `Redis#persist`    | `Boolean`  | Removes the expiry from the key                     |
| `Redis#ttl`        | `Duration` | Returns the remaining time to live, in seconds      |
| `Redis#pTtl`       | `Duration` | Returns the remaining time to live, in milliseconds |

The setters return `false` when the key does not exist, and `Redis#persist` returns `false` when the key has no expiry. To expire a key in an hour and read what is left:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def expireInAnHour(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Duration] =
  for {
    _         <- redis.expire("session:1", 1.hour)
    remaining <- redis.ttl("session:1")
  } yield remaining
```

To expire a key at a fixed point in time with millisecond precision:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._
import java.time.Instant

def expireAtMidnight(redis: Redis, midnight: Instant): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.pExpireAt("daily:report", midnight)
```

### Renaming and Moving

These commands change the name or location of a key:

| Command          | Result    | Description                                                      |
| ---------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#rename`   | `Unit`    | Renames a key and overwrites the target; fails if the key is missing |
| `Redis#renameNx` | `Boolean` | Renames a key only when the new name does not exist              |
| `Redis#copy`     | `Boolean` | Copies a value to another key, optionally into another database  |
| `Redis#move`     | `Boolean` | Moves a key to another database by index                         |

`Redis#copy` takes two optional parameters: `database: Option[Long]` selects the target database, and `replace: Option[Replace]` overwrites an existing target. `Replace` is a single case object. To copy a key and overwrite the target:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def duplicate(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.copy("template", "instance", replace = Some(Replace))
```

### Searching and Scanning

`Redis#keys` returns every key that matches a glob-style pattern, while `Redis#scan` walks the key space in small steps:

| Command        | Result                   | Description                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#keys`   | `Chunk[A]`               | Returns all keys matching a pattern               |
| `Redis#scan`   | `(Long, Chunk[A])`       | Returns the next cursor and one batch of keys     |

`Redis#keys` blocks the server while it scans everything, so prefer `Redis#scan` on large databases. `Redis#scan` takes a cursor and these optional parameters:

| Parameter  | Type                | Effect                                         |
| ---------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `pattern`  | `Option[String]`    | Keeps only keys that match the pattern         |
| `count`    | `Option[Count]`     | Hints how many keys to return per call         |
| `type`     | `Option[RedisType]` | Keeps only keys that hold the given type       |

Iteration starts with cursor `0` and ends when the server returns cursor `0`. To collect every hash key whose name starts with `user:`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def allUsers(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] = {
  def loop(cursor: Long, acc: Chunk[String]): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] =
    redis
      .scan(cursor, Some("user:*"), Some(Count(100L)), Some(RedisType.Hash))
      .returning[String]
      .flatMap { case (next, keys) =>
        val all = acc ++ keys
        if (next == 0L) ZIO.succeed(all) else loop(next, all)
      }

  loop(0L, Chunk.empty)
}
```

### Sorting

`Redis#sort` sorts a list, set or sorted set and returns the values. `Redis#sortStore` runs the same command but stores the result under a key and returns how many values it stored. Both take these parameters:

| Parameter | Type                              | Effect                                                    |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `by`      | `Option[String]`                  | Sorts by the values of external keys that match a pattern |
| `limit`   | `Option[Limit]`                   | Takes `Limit(offset, count)` values from the sorted result |
| `order`   | `Order`                           | `Order.Ascending` (default) or `Order.Descending`         |
| `get`     | `Option[(String, List[String])]`  | Returns the values of external keys instead of the elements |
| `alpha`   | `Option[Alpha]`                   | Sorts alphabetically instead of numerically               |

`Redis#sortStore` takes an extra `storeAt: Store` after the key, where `Store(key)` names the target key. To sort a list of names alphabetically and keep the first ten:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def topNames(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] =
  redis
    .sort("names", limit = Some(Limit(0L, 10L)), order = Order.Descending, alpha = Some(Alpha))
    .returning[String]
```

To store the sorted result under another key:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def storeSorted(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.sortStore("scores", Store("scores:sorted"))
```

### Serialization and Migration

`Redis#dump` and `Redis#restore` copy a value as an opaque, Redis-specific byte string, and `Redis#migrate` moves keys to another server:

| Command          | Result        | Description                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Redis#dump`     | `Chunk[Byte]` | Returns the serialized value of a key                        |
| `Redis#restore`  | `Unit`        | Creates a key from a serialized value                        |
| `Redis#migrate`  | `String`      | Transfers one or more keys to another instance               |

`Redis#restore` takes the time to live as a `Long` in milliseconds, where `0` means no expiry, and these optional parameters:

| Parameter  | Type                | Effect                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `replace`  | `Option[Replace]`   | Overwrites an existing key                              |
| `absTtl`   | `Option[AbsTtl]`    | Treats the time to live as an absolute Unix time in ms  |
| `idleTime` | `Option[IdleTime]`  | Sets the idle time, with `IdleTime(seconds)`            |
| `freq`     | `Option[Freq]`      | Sets the access frequency, with `Freq(frequency)`       |

To copy a value through a dump and restore it under another key:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def cloneValue(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Unit] =
  for {
    bytes <- redis.dump("source")
    _     <- redis.restore("target", 0L, bytes, replace = Some(Replace))
  } yield ()
```

`Redis#migrate` takes the remote `host`, `port`, `key`, `destinationDb` and `timeout`. Its optional parameters are `auth: Option[Auth]`, `copy: Option[Copy]` and `replace: Option[Replace]`. `Auth(username, password)` carries an optional username. The last parameter, `keys: Option[(K, List[K])]`, has no default and must always be passed. To send one key to another server and keep the local copy:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def migrateKey(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, String] =
  redis.migrate(
    host = "replica.example.com",
    port = 6379L,
    key = "report",
    destinationDb = 0L,
    timeout = 5.seconds,
    auth = Some(Auth(None, "secret")),
    copy = Some(Copy),
    keys = None
  )
```

### Waiting for Replicas

`Redis#wait_` blocks until previous writes reach a number of replicas, or until the timeout passes. The method name ends in an underscore because `wait` is reserved on `Object`. It returns how many replicas acknowledged the writes. A `Duration.Zero` timeout blocks forever. To wait for two replicas for at most a second:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def replicated(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  for {
    _        <- redis.set("important", "value")
    replicas <- redis.wait_(2L, 1.second)
  } yield replicas
```

---

## Lists

A Redis list is an ordered sequence of values that supports fast pushes and pops at both ends. This page lists every list command on `Redis`, together with the option types `Side`, `Position`, `Rank` and `ListMaxLen`.

Keys and elements are encoded with the configured [`CodecSupplier`](../../concepts/codecs.md). Commands that return elements end with `returning[A]`, as described in [Getting Started](../../getting-started.md).

### Command Overview

| Purpose              | Commands                                                              |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Push                 | `Redis#lPush`, `Redis#rPush`, `Redis#lPushX`, `Redis#rPushX`          |
| Pop                  | `Redis#lPop`, `Redis#rPop`                                            |
| Blocking pop         | `Redis#blPop`, `Redis#brPop`                                          |
| Move between lists   | `Redis#lMove`, `Redis#blMove`                                         |
| Read                 | `Redis#lIndex`, `Redis#lRange`, `Redis#lLen`                          |
| Search               | `Redis#lPos`, `Redis#lPosCount`                                       |
| Modify               | `Redis#lSet`, `Redis#lInsert`, `Redis#lRem`, `Redis#lTrim`            |

### Option Types

The option types come from `zio.redis._`:

| Type         | Values or shape                          | Used by                                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `Side`       | `Side.Left`, `Side.Right`                | `Redis#lMove`, `Redis#blMove`             |
| `Position`   | `Position.Before`, `Position.After`      | `Redis#lInsert`                           |
| `Rank`       | `Rank(rank: Long)`                       | `Redis#lPos`, `Redis#lPosCount`           |
| `ListMaxLen` | `ListMaxLen(count: Long)`                | `Redis#lPos`, `Redis#lPosCount`           |
| `Count`      | `Count(count: Long)`                     | `Redis#lPosCount`                         |

### Pushing and Popping

`Redis#lPush` prepends and `Redis#rPush` appends. Both accept several elements, create the list if needed, and return the new length. `Redis#lPushX` and `Redis#rPushX` do the same but do nothing when the list does not exist. `Redis#lPop` and `Redis#rPop` remove one element and return an `Option`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def queue(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  for {
    _    <- redis.rPush("jobs", "a", "b", "c")
    _    <- redis.lPushX("jobs", "urgent")
    head <- redis.lPop("jobs").returning[String]
  } yield head
```

### Blocking Pops

`Redis#blPop` and `Redis#brPop` wait until one of the given lists has an element. The timeout is in a second parameter list, and a zero duration blocks indefinitely. The result is `Option[(K, V)]`, holding the key that supplied the element, or `None` when the timeout expires:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def worker(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[(String, String)]] =
  redis.blPop("high", "low")(5.seconds).returning[String]
```

### Moving Elements

`Redis#lMove` atomically pops from one side of a source list and pushes onto one side of a destination list. `Redis#blMove` is the blocking form and takes a `timeout: Duration` as its last argument. Both return an `Option` with the moved element:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def claim(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  for {
    _     <- redis.lMove("pending", "working", Side.Left, Side.Right).returning[String]
    moved <- redis.blMove("pending", "working", Side.Left, Side.Right, 1.second).returning[String]
  } yield moved
```

### Reading Elements

`Redis#lIndex` returns the element at a zero-based index, where negative indices count from the tail. `Redis#lRange` takes a Scala `Range` and returns a `Chunk`. Redis treats `-1` as the last element, so `0 to -1` selects the whole list. `Redis#lLen` returns the length:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def peek(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Option[String], Chunk[String])] =
  for {
    size  <- redis.lLen("jobs")
    last  <- redis.lIndex("jobs", -1L).returning[String]
    first <- redis.lRange("jobs", 0 to 9).returning[String]
  } yield (size, last, first)
```

### Searching

`Redis#lPos` returns the index of the first match as an `Option[Long]`. `Redis#lPosCount` takes a required `Count` and returns up to that many indexes as a `Chunk[Long]`. Both accept an optional `Rank` to select the nth match and an optional `ListMaxLen` to limit comparisons:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def find(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Option[Long], Chunk[Long])] =
  for {
    first <- redis.lPos("jobs", "b")
    all   <- redis.lPosCount("jobs", "b", Count(10L), Some(Rank(1L)), Some(ListMaxLen(1000L)))
  } yield (first, all)
```

### Modifying a List

| Method                                          | Effect                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#lSet(key, index, element)`               | Replaces the element at an index                                     |
| `Redis#lInsert(key, position, pivot, element)`  | Inserts next to the first `pivot`, returns the new length or `-1`    |
| `Redis#lRem(key, count, element)`               | Removes matching elements and returns how many were removed          |
| `Redis#lTrim(key, range)`                       | Keeps only the elements in the range                                 |

For `Redis#lRem`, a positive `count` removes from the head, a negative one from the tail, and zero removes all matches. The `element` parameter is a `String`, not a generic value:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def tidy(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  for {
    _       <- redis.lSet("jobs", 0L, "first")
    _       <- redis.lInsert("jobs", Position.After, "first", "second")
    removed <- redis.lRem("jobs", 0L, "stale")
    _       <- redis.lTrim("jobs", 0 to 99)
  } yield removed
```

### Next Steps

- [Sets](./sets.md) stores unique members without order.
- [Streams](./streams.md) offers consumer groups for work queues.
- [Keys](./keys.md) covers expiry for list keys.

## Scripting

Redis can run Lua scripts on the server. A script runs atomically, so no other command executes while it runs. This page covers the seven scripting commands on `Redis`.

The library has no `MULTI`, `EXEC`, `DISCARD` or `WATCH` commands and no transaction API, so atomic multi-step logic is written as a Lua script and run with `Redis#eval` or `Redis#evalSha`.

### Running Scripts

`Redis#eval` sends the script text, a `Chunk` of keys that the script reads through `KEYS`, and a `Chunk` of arguments that it reads through `ARGV`. The following table lists the commands that run scripts:

| Command          | Purpose                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#eval`     | Runs a script sent as text                               |
| `Redis#evalSha`  | Runs a script already cached on the server, by its SHA1  |

Both commands finish with `returning[R]`, but unlike the other commands they do not use a ZIO Schema `Schema`. They require an `Input[K]` for the keys, an `Input[A]` for the arguments and an `Output[R]` for the result, and the library provides no implicit instances of these. We define them ourselves from the public building blocks in `Input` and `Output`, such as `StringInput`, `LongInput`, `LongOutput`, `MultiStringOutput` and `ChunkOutput`.

The following example defines the instances in an object and increments a counter only when it is below a limit. The script runs atomically, so concurrent callers cannot exceed the limit:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

object ScriptCodecs {
  implicit val stringInput: Input[String] = Input.StringInput
  implicit val longInput: Input[Long]     = Input.LongInput
  implicit val longOutput: Output[Long]   = Output.LongOutput
}

import ScriptCodecs._

val incrementBelowLimit: String =
  """local current = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or '0')
    |if current < tonumber(ARGV[1]) then
    |  return redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])
    |end
    |return -1""".stripMargin

def increment(redis: Redis, limit: Long): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.eval(incrementBelowLimit, Chunk("counter"), Chunk(limit)).returning[Long]
```

The script's return value is converted by the `Output` you choose, so it must match the Lua type: a number needs `LongOutput`, a string `MultiStringOutput`, and a table `ChunkOutput` of an element output. A mismatch fails with a `RedisError`.

### Caching Scripts

Sending the whole script on every call wastes bandwidth. `Redis#scriptLoad` stores the script in the server's script cache and returns its SHA1 digest, which `Redis#evalSha` accepts in place of the text. The following example loads a script once and then runs it by digest:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

object ShaCodecs {
  implicit val stringInput: Input[String]  = Input.StringInput
  implicit val stringOutput: Output[String] = Output.MultiStringOutput
}

import ShaCodecs._

def runCached(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, String] =
  for {
    sha    <- redis.scriptLoad("return ARGV[1]")
    result <- redis.evalSha(sha, Chunk.empty[String], Chunk("hello")).returning[String]
  } yield result
```

The cache is not persistent. After a server restart or `Redis#scriptFlush`, `Redis#evalSha` fails with a `NOSCRIPT` error, so a program that relies on it should load the script again and retry.

### Managing the Script Cache

The following table lists the commands that manage the cache and running scripts:

| Command                | Parameters                          | Returns          |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `Redis#scriptLoad`     | `script: String`                    | The SHA1 digest  |
| `Redis#scriptExists`   | `sha1: String, sha1s: String*`      | `Chunk[Boolean]` |
| `Redis#scriptFlush`    | `mode: Option[FlushMode] = None`    | `Unit`           |
| `Redis#scriptKill`     | none                                | `Unit`           |
| `Redis#scriptDebug`    | `mode: DebugMode`                   | `Unit`           |

`Redis#scriptExists` returns one `Boolean` per digest, in the order given. `Redis#scriptKill` stops the running script, and Redis refuses when the script has already written data. The following example flushes the cache only when a script is missing:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def flushIfMissing(redis: Redis, sha: String): IO[RedisError, Unit] =
  redis.scriptExists(sha).flatMap { found =>
    ZIO.unless(found.forall(identity))(redis.scriptFlush(Some(FlushMode.Async))).unit
  }
```

### Option Types

`FlushMode` selects how `Redis#scriptFlush` clears the cache. When no mode is given, the server uses its default, which is synchronous:

| Value             | Behavior                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `FlushMode.Async` | Flushes the cache in the background   |
| `FlushMode.Sync`  | Flushes the cache and waits           |

`DebugMode` configures the Lua debugger for scripts run afterwards with `Redis#eval`:

| Value            | Behavior                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DebugMode.Yes`  | Non-blocking debugging; changes made by the script are discarded |
| `DebugMode.Sync` | Blocking debugging; changes made by the script are saved       |
| `DebugMode.No`   | Turns debugging off                                            |

The following example turns the debugger off:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def stopDebugging(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Unit] =
  redis.scriptDebug(DebugMode.No)
```

### Related Pages

- [Keys](./keys.md) and [Strings](./strings.md) cover the commands a script usually calls.
- [Error Handling](../../concepts/error-handling.md) lists the errors raised by failing scripts.

## Sets

A Redis set is an unordered collection of unique members. This page lists every set command on `Redis`, grouped by what it does.

Members and keys are encoded with the configured [`CodecSupplier`](../../concepts/codecs.md). Commands that return members end with `returning[A]`, as described in [Getting Started](../../getting-started.md).

### Command Overview

| Purpose              | Commands                                                                |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Add and remove       | `Redis#sAdd`, `Redis#sRem`, `Redis#sPop`, `Redis#sMove`                 |
| Inspect              | `Redis#sCard`, `Redis#sIsMember`, `Redis#sMembers`, `Redis#sRandMember` |
| Combine, return      | `Redis#sUnion`, `Redis#sInter`, `Redis#sDiff`                           |
| Combine, store       | `Redis#sUnionStore`, `Redis#sInterStore`, `Redis#sDiffStore`            |
| Iterate              | `Redis#sScan`                                                           |

### Adding and Removing Members

`Redis#sAdd` and `Redis#sRem` accept one or more members. `Redis#sAdd` returns the number of members that were newly added, and `Redis#sRem` returns the number that were actually removed:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def editTags(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Long)] =
  for {
    added   <- redis.sAdd("tags", "scala", "zio", "redis")
    removed <- redis.sRem("tags", "redis", "missing")
  } yield (added, removed)
```

`Redis#sMove(source, destination, member)` moves a member between two sets and returns `true` if the member was found in the source:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def archive(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.sMove("tags", "archived-tags", "zio")
```

### Inspecting a Set

These commands read a set without changing it:

| Method                              | Returns      | Meaning                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#sCard(key)`                  | `Long`       | Number of members, or zero if the key is missing |
| `Redis#sIsMember(key, member)`      | `Boolean`    | Whether the member is in the set              |
| `Redis#sMembers(key)`               | `Chunk[A]`   | All members                                   |

To read the members and check one of them:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def inspect(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Boolean, Chunk[String])] =
  for {
    size    <- redis.sCard("tags")
    isScala <- redis.sIsMember("tags", "scala")
    members <- redis.sMembers("tags").returning[String]
  } yield (size, isScala, members)
```

### Random Members

`Redis#sPop` removes random members, and `Redis#sRandMember` returns them without removing. Both take an optional `count: Option[Long]` and always return a `Chunk`, even when `count` is `None`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def pickWinners(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Chunk[String], Chunk[String])] =
  for {
    peek   <- redis.sRandMember("entries", Some(2L)).returning[String]
    winner <- redis.sPop("entries", Some(1L)).returning[String]
  } yield (peek, winner)
```

### Combining Sets

Each operation has two forms. The first returns the resulting members, and the second writes them to a destination key and returns the size of the new set:

| Operation    | Returns members                   | Stores result                                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Union        | `Redis#sUnion(key, keys*)`        | `Redis#sUnionStore(destination, key, keys*)`         |
| Intersection | `Redis#sInter(key, keys*)`        | `Redis#sInterStore(destination, key, keys*)`         |
| Difference   | `Redis#sDiff(key, keys*)`         | `Redis#sDiffStore(destination, key, keys*)`          |

`Redis#sDiff` subtracts every later set from the first one, so the order of keys matters. To compute set algebra over two sets:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def combine(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Chunk[String], Chunk[String], Long)] =
  for {
    both   <- redis.sInter("scala-devs", "zio-devs").returning[String]
    onlyA  <- redis.sDiff("scala-devs", "zio-devs").returning[String]
    stored <- redis.sUnionStore("all-devs", "scala-devs", "zio-devs")
  } yield (both, onlyA, stored)
```

### Scanning

`Redis#sScan` iterates the members with a cursor. Start from `0` and continue with the returned cursor until it is `0` again. The optional `pattern` is a glob-style filter and `count` is a `Count` hint:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def scanTags(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] = {
  def loop(cursor: Long, acc: Chunk[String]): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] =
    redis.sScan("tags", cursor, Some("s*"), Some(Count(50L))).returning[String].flatMap {
      case (0L, items)   => ZIO.succeed(acc ++ items)
      case (next, items) => loop(next, acc ++ items)
    }

  loop(0L, Chunk.empty)
}
```

### Next Steps

- [Sorted Sets](./sorted-sets.md) adds a score to every member.
- [Lists](./lists.md) keeps insertion order and allows duplicates.
- [Hashes](./hashes.md) stores field and value pairs.

## Sorted Sets

A sorted set stores unique members, each with a floating point score, and keeps them ordered by score. This page documents the sorted set commands of ZIO Redis and the option types they accept.

All commands are methods on the `Redis` service. Keys and members are encoded with the configured [`CodecSupplier`](../../concepts/codecs.md). Commands that return members need `returning[A]`, as explained in [Getting Started](../../getting-started.md).

### Commands

The commands are grouped below by purpose:

| Group          | Methods                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Add and update | `Redis#zAdd`, `Redis#zAddWithIncr`, `Redis#zIncrBy`                                                      |
| Size and score | `Redis#zCard`, `Redis#zCount`, `Redis#zLexCount`, `Redis#zScore`, `Redis#zMScore`                        |
| Rank           | `Redis#zRank`, `Redis#zRankWithScore`, `Redis#zRevRank`, `Redis#zRevRankWithScore`                       |
| Range queries  | `Redis#zRange`, `Redis#zRangeWithScores`, `Redis#zRangeStore`                                            |
| Random members | `Redis#zRandMember`, `Redis#zRandMemberWithScores`                                                       |
| Remove         | `Redis#zRem`, `Redis#zRemRangeByLex`, `Redis#zRemRangeByRank`, `Redis#zRemRangeByScore`                  |
| Pop            | `Redis#zPopMin`, `Redis#zPopMax`, `Redis#zmPopMin`, `Redis#zmPopMax`                                     |
| Blocking pop   | `Redis#bzPopMin`, `Redis#bzPopMax`, `Redis#bZmPopMin`, `Redis#bZmPopMax`                                 |
| Set algebra    | `Redis#zDiff`, `Redis#zDiffWithScores`, `Redis#zDiffStore`, `Redis#zInter`, `Redis#zInterWithScores`, `Redis#zInterStore`, `Redis#zInterCard`, `Redis#zUnion`, `Redis#zUnionWithScores`, `Redis#zUnionStore` |
| Iteration      | `Redis#zScan`                                                                                            |

The deprecated methods `Redis#zRevRangeWithScores`, `Redis#zRangeByScoreWithScores` and `Redis#zRevRangeByScoreWithScores`, and the overloads of `Redis#zRange` and `Redis#zRangeWithScores` that take a Scala `Range`, are replaced by the `SortedSetRange` versions described below.

### Option Types

The following types are available after `import zio.redis._`:

| Type                | Shape                                                                       | Used by                                   |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `MemberScore[M]`    | `MemberScore(member: M, score: Double)`                                     | `zAdd` and every `WithScores` result      |
| `RankScore`         | `RankScore(rank: Long, score: Double)`                                      | `zRankWithScore`, `zRevRankWithScore`     |
| `Update`            | `SetExisting` (`XX`), `SetNew` (`NX`), `SetLessThan` (`LT`), `SetGreaterThan` (`GT`) | `zAdd`, `zAddWithIncr`            |
| `Changed`           | Singleton `Changed`, makes the result count changed members                 | `zAdd`, `zAddWithIncr`                    |
| `Increment`         | Singleton `Increment`, makes `ZADD` act like `ZINCRBY`                      | `zAddWithIncr`                            |
| `Aggregate`         | `Aggregate.Sum`, `Aggregate.Min` or `Aggregate.Max`                         | `zInter*`, `zUnion*`                      |
| `Limit`             | `Limit(offset: Long, count: Long)`                                          | `zRange`, `zRangeWithScores`, `zRangeStore` |
| `Count`             | `Count(count: Long)`                                                        | `zScan`                                   |
| `SortedSetRange`    | `Range`, `ScoreRange` or `LexRange`                                         | `zRange`, `zRangeWithScores`, `zRangeStore` |

`SortedSetRange` has three cases, and each one carries its own bound types:

| Case                                  | Bound types                                                                                   | Queries by |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `SortedSetRange.Range(min, max)`      | `RangeMinimum(value: Long)`, `RangeMaximum.Inclusive(value)`, `RangeMaximum.Exclusive(value)`  | Rank       |
| `SortedSetRange.ScoreRange(min, max)` | `ScoreMinimum.Closed`, `ScoreMinimum.Open`, `ScoreMinimum.Infinity`, `ScoreMaximum.Closed`, `ScoreMaximum.Open`, `ScoreMaximum.Infinity` | Score |
| `SortedSetRange.LexRange(min, max)`   | `LexMinimum.Closed`, `LexMinimum.Open`, `LexMinimum.UnboundedNegative`, `LexMinimum.UnboundedPositive`, and the same four on `LexMaximum` | Lexicographic order |

`Closed` includes the bound and `Open` excludes it. `ScoreMinimum.Infinity` means `-inf` and `ScoreMaximum.Infinity` means `+inf`. For lexicographic bounds, `UnboundedNegative` is `-` and `UnboundedPositive` is `+`.

### Adding and Updating Members

`Redis#zAdd` adds members with scores and returns the number of new members. The optional `update` parameter restricts the write, and `change` makes the result count every member whose score changed:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def addScores(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.zAdd("leaderboard", Some(Update.SetNew), Some(Changed))(
    MemberScore("alice", 120.0),
    MemberScore("bob", 95.5)
  )
```

`Redis#zAddWithIncr` adds the given score to the existing one and returns the new score, or `None` if an `update` condition aborted the write. `Redis#zIncrBy` does the same with a whole number increment and always returns the new score:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def bumpScores(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Option[Double], Double)] =
  for {
    a <- redis.zAddWithIncr("leaderboard")(Increment, MemberScore("alice", 10.0))
    b <- redis.zIncrBy("leaderboard", 5L, "bob")
  } yield (a, b)
```

### Size, Score and Rank

The size and score commands answer questions without returning members. `Redis#zCount` takes a Scala `Range` of whole number scores, and `Redis#zLexCount` takes a `SortedSetRange.LexRange`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def sizes(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Long, Long)] =
  for {
    total   <- redis.zCard("leaderboard")
    inScore <- redis.zCount("leaderboard", 0 to 100)
    inLex   <- redis.zLexCount("names", SortedSetRange.LexRange(LexMinimum.Closed("a"), LexMaximum.Open("n")))
  } yield (total, inScore, inLex)
```

`Redis#zScore` returns the score of one member, and `Redis#zMScore` returns one optional score per member. Its first argument is the sorted set key, followed by the members, and all of them share the single type `K`. The rank commands return `None` for a missing member, and the `Rev` variants count from the highest score:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def lookups(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Option[Double], Option[Long], Option[RankScore])] =
  for {
    score <- redis.zScore("leaderboard", "alice")
    rank  <- redis.zRank("leaderboard", "alice")
    both  <- redis.zRevRankWithScore("leaderboard", "alice")
  } yield (score, rank, both)
```

### Range Queries

`Redis#zRange` and `Redis#zRangeWithScores` take a `SortedSetRange`, an optional `rev` flag and an optional `Limit`. The first returns members, and the second returns `MemberScore` values. To read the top three members by rank, with scores:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def topThree(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[MemberScore[String]]] =
  redis
    .zRangeWithScores(
      "leaderboard",
      SortedSetRange.Range(RangeMinimum(0L), RangeMaximum.Inclusive(2L)),
      rev = true
    )
    .returning[String]
```

To query by score and page through the matches, use `SortedSetRange.ScoreRange` with a `Limit`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def byScore(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[String]] =
  redis
    .zRange(
      "leaderboard",
      SortedSetRange.ScoreRange(ScoreMinimum.Closed(50.0), ScoreMaximum.Infinity),
      limit = Some(Limit(0L, 10L))
    )
    .returning[String]
```

When `rev` is `true`, the bounds are still given as minimum then maximum, and the library reorders them for score and lexicographic queries. To copy a range into another key, use `Redis#zRangeStore`, which returns the size of the destination:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def copyRange(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.zRangeStore(
    "leaderboard:top",
    "leaderboard",
    SortedSetRange.Range(RangeMinimum(0L), RangeMaximum.Inclusive(9L)),
    rev = true
  )
```

### Random Members

`Redis#zRandMember(key)` returns an `Option` of one member. The overload with a `count` returns a `Chunk`, and `Redis#zRandMemberWithScores` includes the scores. A negative count allows repeated members:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def sample(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Option[String], Chunk[MemberScore[String]])] =
  for {
    one  <- redis.zRandMember("leaderboard").returning[String]
    many <- redis.zRandMemberWithScores("leaderboard", 3L).returning[String]
  } yield (one, many)
```

### Removing Members

The remove commands return the number of members removed. `Redis#zRemRangeByRank` takes a Scala `Range`, `Redis#zRemRangeByScore` takes a `SortedSetRange.ScoreRange`, and `Redis#zRemRangeByLex` takes a `SortedSetRange.LexRange`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def prune(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  for {
    a <- redis.zRem("leaderboard", "bob", "carol")
    b <- redis.zRemRangeByRank("leaderboard", 0 to 1)
    c <- redis.zRemRangeByScore("leaderboard", SortedSetRange.ScoreRange(ScoreMinimum.Infinity, ScoreMaximum.Open(10.0)))
  } yield a + b + c
```

### Popping Members

`Redis#zPopMin` and `Redis#zPopMax` remove members from a single key and return them with their scores. `Redis#zmPopMin` and `Redis#zmPopMax` take several keys and pop from the first non-empty one, returning that key together with the popped members. The `count` is the first parameter list:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def popLowest(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[(String, Chunk[MemberScore[String]])]] =
  redis.zmPopMin(Some(2L))("queue:high", "queue:low").returning[String]
```

### Blocking Pops

The blocking variants wait until a member is available or the `timeout` expires. `Redis#bzPopMin` and `Redis#bzPopMax` return the key and a single `MemberScore`, and `Redis#bZmPopMin` and `Redis#bZmPopMax` mirror `zmPopMin` and `zmPopMax` with a timeout. All of them return `None` when the timeout expires:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def nextJob(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[(String, MemberScore[String])]] =
  redis.bzPopMin(5.seconds, "queue:high", "queue:low").returning[String]
```

### Set Algebra

The set algebra commands combine several sorted sets. Each family has a plain form that returns members, a `WithScores` form that returns `MemberScore` values, and a `Store` form that writes into a destination key and returns its size. `Redis#zDiff` has no weights or aggregate, while `Redis#zInter` and `Redis#zUnion` accept both, and `Redis#zInterCard` only counts. The weights have the type `Option[::[Double]]`, a non-empty list with one weight per input key:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def combine(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Chunk[MemberScore[String]], Long, Long)] =
  for {
    inter <- redis
               .zInterWithScores("scores:a", "scores:b")(Some(Aggregate.Max), Some(::(2.0, List(1.0))))
               .returning[String]
    union <- redis.zUnionStore("scores:all", "scores:a", "scores:b")(None, Some(Aggregate.Sum))
    card  <- redis.zInterCard(Some(100L))("scores:a", "scores:b")
  } yield (inter, union, card)
```

Note that `Redis#zInter` takes `aggregate` before `weights`, while `Redis#zUnion` and `Redis#zUnionStore` take `weights` before `aggregate`. `Redis#zDiffStore` takes the destination first, then the source keys.

### Iterating

`Redis#zScan` walks a sorted set in batches. Start with cursor `0L`, and continue with the returned cursor until it is `0L` again. The optional `pattern` filters members, and `count` is a hint for the batch size:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def scanAll(redis: Redis, cursor: Long = 0L): IO[RedisError, Chunk[MemberScore[String]]] =
  redis.zScan("leaderboard", cursor, Some("a*"), Some(Count(100L))).returning[String].flatMap {
    case (0L, batch)   => ZIO.succeed(batch)
    case (next, batch) => scanAll(redis, next).map(batch ++ _)
  }
```

### Next Steps

- [Geo](./geo.md) builds on sorted sets to store coordinates.
- [Sets](./sets.md) covers unordered unique members.
- [Keys](./keys.md) covers expiry and deletion for sorted set keys.

## Streams

A Redis stream is an append-only log of entries, each made of an ID and a set of field-value pairs. This page covers the 32 stream commands on `Redis`, from appending and reading entries to consumer groups, claiming and trimming.

Stream IDs have the form `<milliseconds>-<sequence>`. Pass `"*"` to `Redis#xAdd` to let the server generate the ID, and use `"-"` and `"+"` as the smallest and largest possible IDs in range queries.

Every command here takes the key, group, consumer and ID as values with a ZIO Schema `Schema`, which are encoded by the [`CodecSupplier`](../../concepts/codecs.md). In the examples they are plain `String`s.

### Appending Entries

`Redis#xAdd` appends an entry made of one or more field-value pairs. The result type is the type of the generated ID, so we finish with `returning[A]`, and the result is `None` when `noMakeStream` is set and the stream does not exist:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def addClick(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  redis.xAdd("clicks", "*")("page" -> "/home", "user" -> "42").returning[String]
```

The following table lists the commands that append entries:

| Command                  | Purpose                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#xAdd`             | Appends an entry                                                  |
| `Redis#xAddWithMaxLen`   | Appends an entry and trims the stream to at most `count` entries  |
| `Redis#xAddWithMinId`    | Appends an entry and evicts entries with an ID lower than `minId` |

`Redis#xAddWithMaxLen` and `Redis#xAddWithMinId` take the same `approximate` and `limit` parameters, described under [Trimming Streams](#capped-streams). The following example keeps roughly the latest 1000 entries:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def addCapped(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  redis
    .xAddWithMaxLen("clicks", "*", count = 1000L, approximate = true)("page" -> "/home")
    .returning[String]
```

### Reading Entries

Range queries return the entries between two IDs, inclusive. They return `StreamEntries[I, K, V]`, which is a `Chunk[StreamEntry[I, K, V]]`, where `StreamEntry` holds an `id` and a `fields` map:

| Command             | Purpose                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Redis#xRange`      | Returns entries from `start` to `end`, optionally `count`    |
| `Redis#xRevRange`   | Returns entries from `end` down to `start`, optionally `count` |
| `Redis#xLen`        | Returns the number of entries                                |
| `Redis#xDel`        | Deletes entries by ID and returns how many were deleted      |

Note that `Redis#xRevRange` takes `end` before `start`. The following example reads the ten oldest entries:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def firstTen(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, StreamEntries[String, String, String]] =
  redis.xRange("clicks", "-", "+", 10L).returning[String, String]
```

`Redis#xRead` reads from one or more streams, starting after the given ID in each. Pass `"0-0"` to read from the beginning, or `"$"` together with `block` to wait for entries that arrive later. It returns `StreamChunks[SK, I, K, V]`, a `Chunk[StreamChunk]` with the stream `name` and its `entries`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def waitForNew(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, StreamChunks[String, String, String, String]] =
  redis.xRead(count = Some(10L), block = Some(5.seconds))("clicks" -> "$").returning[String, String]
```

### Capped Streams

A stream grows without bound unless it is capped. The trimming commands and options use `CappedStreamType` internally, with the cases `MaxLenApprox`, `MaxLenExact`, `MinIdApprox` and `MinIdExact`. Public methods expose the same choice through plain parameters.

| Command                  | Trims by                          |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `Redis#xTrimWithMaxLen`  | Number of entries (`threshold`)   |
| `Redis#xTrimWithMinId`   | Smallest ID to keep (`threshold`) |

Both commands take `approximate: Boolean = false` and `limit: Option[Long] = None`. With `approximate = true`, Redis may keep slightly more entries than requested, which is cheaper, and `limit` bounds the work done per call. Both return the number of entries removed:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def trim(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.xTrimWithMaxLen("clicks", threshold = 10000L, approximate = true, limit = Some(100L))
```

### Consumer Groups

A consumer group lets several consumers share the work of reading one stream. Redis delivers each entry to one consumer of the group and remembers it in the group's pending entries list until the consumer acknowledges it.

The following table lists the commands that manage groups and consumers:

| Command                          | Purpose                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#xGroupCreate`             | Creates a group that starts after the given ID                |
| `Redis#xGroupCreateLastEntry`    | Creates a group that starts after the current last entry      |
| `Redis#xGroupSetId`              | Moves the group's last delivered ID                           |
| `Redis#xGroupSetIdLastEntry`     | Moves the group's last delivered ID to the last entry         |
| `Redis#xGroupDestroy`            | Deletes a group and returns whether it existed                |
| `Redis#xGroupCreateConsumer`     | Creates a consumer and returns whether it was created         |
| `Redis#xGroupDelConsumer`        | Deletes a consumer and returns how many pending entries it had |

`Redis#xGroupCreate` and `Redis#xGroupCreateLastEntry` accept `mkStream: Boolean = false`, which creates the stream when it does not exist, and `entriesRead: Option[Long] = None`. The `*LastEntry` variants pass `"$"` for you. The following example creates a group on a new stream and registers a consumer:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def setUp(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.xGroupCreate("orders", "billing", "0-0", mkStream = true) *>
    redis.xGroupCreateConsumer("orders", "billing", "worker-1")
```

### The Stream Reading Flow

The usual flow with a consumer group has four steps. A producer appends entries with `Redis#xAdd`. A consumer calls `Redis#xReadGroup` with the ID `">"`, which asks for entries never delivered to any consumer of the group. After handling an entry, the consumer calls `Redis#xAck`. Entries that were never acknowledged are recovered with `Redis#xPending`, `Redis#xClaim` or `Redis#xAutoClaim`.

`Redis#xReadGroup` takes `count`, `block` and `noAck`. With `noAck = true` entries are not added to the pending list, so no acknowledgement is needed. If you pass an ID such as `"0"` instead of `">"`, Redis returns the consumer's own pending entries.

`Redis#xAck` takes a group and one or more IDs and returns how many entries were acknowledged. The following example reads a batch, handles each entry and acknowledges it:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def consume(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Unit] =
  for {
    chunks <- redis
                .xReadGroup("billing", "worker-1", count = Some(10L), block = Some(2.seconds))("orders" -> ">")
                .returning[String, String]
    _      <- ZIO.foreachDiscard(chunks.flatMap(_.entries)) { entry =>
                ZIO.debug(s"handling ${entry.id}: ${entry.fields}") *>
                  redis.xAck("orders", "billing", entry.id)
              }
  } yield ()
```

### Recovering Pending Entries

When a consumer crashes, its entries stay in the pending list. The following table lists the commands that inspect and take over pending entries:

| Command                         | Purpose                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#xPending` (group only)   | Returns a `PendingInfo` summary                                  |
| `Redis#xPending` (with range)   | Returns a `Chunk[PendingMessage]` for a range of IDs             |
| `Redis#xClaim`                  | Transfers named entries to a consumer and returns them           |
| `Redis#xClaimWithJustId`        | Same, but returns only the IDs                                   |
| `Redis#xAutoClaim`              | Scans the pending list and claims idle entries, returning them   |
| `Redis#xAutoClaimWithJustId`    | Same, but returns only the IDs                                   |

`PendingInfo` holds `total`, the `first` and `last` pending IDs and a `consumers` map of pending counts. Each `PendingMessage` holds `id`, `owner`, `lastDelivered` and `counter`. The ranged `Redis#xPending` also accepts `consumer: Option[SC]` and `idle: Option[Duration]` to filter the result:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def inspect(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (PendingInfo, Chunk[PendingMessage])] =
  for {
    summary <- redis.xPending("orders", "billing")
    details <- redis.xPending("orders", "billing", "-", "+", 10L, Some("worker-1"), Some(1.minute))
  } yield (summary, details)
```

`Redis#xClaim` takes the `minIdleTime` an entry must have exceeded, plus the optional `idle`, `time`, `retryCount`, `force` and `lastId` parameters that set the new delivery state. `Redis#xAutoClaim` takes `minIdleTime` and an optional `count`, and the `start` ID in the second parameter list. It returns a `StreamClaimedEntries` with `streamId`, the `entries` and the `deletedIds`. The `WithJustId` variant returns a `StreamClaimedIdChunk` with `streamId`, `claimedIds` and `deletedIds`. Use the `streamId` as the next `start`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def takeOver(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, StreamClaimedEntries[String, String, String, String]] =
  redis
    .xAutoClaim("orders", "billing", "worker-2", 5.minutes, count = Some(Count(10L)))("0-0")
    .returning[String, String, String]
```

### Stream Information

The info commands return typed summaries instead of raw replies:

| Command                      | Returns                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#xInfoStream`          | `StreamInfo[I, K, V]` with length, last ID, first and last entry  |
| `Redis#xInfoStreamFull`      | `FullStreamInfo[I, K, V]` with entries, groups and consumers      |
| `Redis#xInfoGroups`          | `Chunk[StreamGroupsInfo]`                                         |
| `Redis#xInfoConsumers`       | `Chunk[StreamConsumersInfo]`                                      |

`Redis#xInfoStreamFull` has an overload that takes `count: Long` to limit the number of entries and pending records reported. The `FullStreamInfo` and its `ConsumerGroups`, `Consumers`, `GroupPel` and `ConsumerPel` types live in `StreamInfoWithFull`. The following example prints the lag of each group:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def lags(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[(String, Long)]] =
  redis.xInfoGroups("orders").map(_.map(g => g.name -> g.lag))
```

### Option Types

The following table summarizes the types from `options/Streams.scala` that appear in command signatures and results:

| Type                                   | Used by                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `StreamEntry[I, K, V]`                 | `id` and `fields: Map[K, V]` of one entry       |
| `StreamChunk[N, I, K, V]`              | Entries of one stream read by `xRead`           |
| `StreamClaimedEntries[SI, I, K, V]`    | Result of `xAutoClaim`                          |
| `StreamClaimedIdChunk[SI, I]`          | Result of `xAutoClaimWithJustId`                |
| `PendingInfo`, `PendingMessage`        | Results of `xPending`                           |
| `StreamInfo`, `StreamGroupsInfo`, `StreamConsumersInfo` | Results of the `xInfo*` commands |

`XGroupCommand`, `WithForce`, `WithJustId`, `MkStream`, `NoMkStream`, `NoAck`, `LastId` and `WithEntriesRead` encode the command arguments for you and are not needed in application code.

### Related Pages

- [Lists](./lists.md) offer a simpler queue when consumer groups are not needed.
- [Codecs](../../concepts/codecs.md) explains how keys, fields and values are encoded.
- [Error Handling](../../concepts/error-handling.md) lists the errors raised, such as `NOGROUP` when a group does not exist.

## Strings

Strings are the simplest Redis value: a byte sequence that can hold text, a number or an encoded case class. This page lists every string command on the `Redis` service, grouped by purpose, with the option types they take.

### Reading and Writing Values

The basic commands read and write one key at a time. Methods that return user data, such as `Redis#get`, finish with `returning[A]`, as explained in [Getting Started](../../getting-started.md):

| Command           | Result                | Description                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Redis#get`       | `Option[A]`           | Returns the value of a key, or `None` when it does not exist |
| `Redis#getDel`    | `Option[A]`           | Returns the value of a key and deletes the key               |
| `Redis#getSet`    | `Option[A]`           | Sets a new value and returns the old one                     |
| `Redis#set`       | `Boolean`             | Sets a value, with optional expiry and condition             |
| `Redis#setGet`    | `Option[V]`           | Like `set`, and returns the old value in the same call       |
| `Redis#setNx`     | `Boolean`             | Sets a value only when the key does not exist                |
| `Redis#append`    | `Long`                | Appends to a value and returns the new length                |
| `Redis#strLen`    | `Long`                | Returns the length of a value                                |
| `Redis#getRange`  | `Option[A]`           | Returns the substring selected by a Scala `Range`            |
| `Redis#setRange`  | `Long`                | Overwrites part of a value from an offset                    |

To write a value and read it back:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def readWrite(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  for {
    _     <- redis.set("greeting", "hello")
    _     <- redis.append("greeting", ", world")
    value <- redis.get("greeting").returning[String]
  } yield value
```

`Redis#getSet` and `Redis#getDel` return the previous value through `returning`, while `Redis#setGet` fixes the result type to the value type `V`. To replace a value and keep the old one:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def swap(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  redis.setGet("token", "new-token")
```

### Conditional Writes and Expiry

`Redis#set` and `Redis#setGet` share the same optional parameters:

| Parameter    | Type               | Effect                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `expireTime` | `Option[Duration]` | Sets a time to live, sent to Redis in milliseconds      |
| `update`     | `Option[Update]`   | Sets the key only if it exists or only if it is missing |
| `keepTtl`    | `Option[KeepTtl]`  | Keeps the time to live the key already has              |

`Update` has four cases. `Update.SetExisting` sends `XX` and `Update.SetNew` sends `NX`. The remaining cases, `Update.SetLessThan` and `Update.SetGreaterThan`, are shared with other commands and are not valid for `SET`. `KeepTtl` is a single case object.

`Redis#set` returns `false` when the condition prevents the write. To store a value only if the key is missing, and keep it for ten minutes:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def acquire(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.set("lock:job", "owner-1", Some(10.minutes), Some(Update.SetNew))
```

To overwrite a value without touching its expiry:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def refresh(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Boolean] =
  redis.set("session", "v2", keepTtl = Some(KeepTtl))
```

Dedicated commands combine a write with an expiry in one call:

| Command         | Result    | Description                                           |
| --------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#setEx`   | `Unit`    | Sets a value that expires after a `Duration`          |
| `Redis#pSetEx`  | `Unit`    | Sets a value that expires after a `Duration`, in ms   |
| `Redis#setNx`   | `Boolean` | Sets a value only when the key does not exist         |

### Reading with an Expiry

`Redis#getEx` reads a value and changes its time to live in one step. It has three overloads:

| Overload                                  | Effect                                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `getEx(key, expire, expireTime)`          | Sets a relative expiry with an `Expire` and `Duration` |
| `getEx(key, expiredAt, timestamp)`        | Sets an absolute expiry with an `ExpiredAt` and `Instant` |
| `getEx(key, persist)`                     | Removes the expiry when `persist` is `true`          |

`Expire` selects the unit of the relative form: `Expire.SetExpireSeconds` sends `EX` and `Expire.SetExpireMilliseconds` sends `PX`. `ExpiredAt` does the same for the absolute form: `ExpiredAt.SetExpireAtSeconds` sends `EXAT` and `ExpiredAt.SetExpireAtMilliseconds` sends `PXAT`.

To read a value and extend its lifetime, then read it and make it permanent:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def touchAndPersist(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  for {
    _     <- redis.getEx("session", Expire.SetExpireSeconds, 30.minutes).returning[String]
    value <- redis.getEx("session", persist = true).returning[String]
  } yield value
```

### Multiple Keys

The multi-key commands take at least one key or pair, followed by any number of extra ones:

| Command         | Result                 | Description                                         |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#mGet`    | `Chunk[Option[A]]`     | Returns the values of several keys                  |
| `Redis#mSet`    | `Unit`                 | Sets several key-value pairs at once                |
| `Redis#mSetNx`  | `Boolean`              | Sets all pairs only if none of the keys exist       |

`Redis#mGet` returns one entry per key, in order, with `None` for missing keys. To set two keys and read them back:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def multi(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[Option[String]]] =
  for {
    _      <- redis.mSet("a" -> "1", "b" -> "2")
    values <- redis.mGet("a", "b", "missing").returning[String]
  } yield values
```

### Counters

Counters treat a value as a 64-bit integer, or as a float for `Redis#incrByFloat`. Redis creates a missing key with the value `0` before applying the change:

| Command              | Result   | Description                              |
| -------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `Redis#incr`         | `Long`   | Adds one and returns the new value       |
| `Redis#incrBy`       | `Long`   | Adds a `Long` and returns the new value  |
| `Redis#incrByFloat`  | `Double` | Adds a `Double` and returns the new value|
| `Redis#decr`         | `Long`   | Subtracts one and returns the new value  |
| `Redis#decrBy`       | `Long`   | Subtracts a `Long` and returns the new value |

To count page views and add a fractional score:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def counters(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Double)] =
  for {
    views <- redis.incr("page:views")
    score <- redis.incrByFloat("page:score", 1.5)
  } yield (views, score)
```

### Bit Operations

Bit commands treat a string as an array of bits. `getBit` and `setBit` address one bit by its offset:

| Command           | Result                  | Description                                            |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Redis#getBit`    | `Long`                  | Returns the bit at an offset                           |
| `Redis#setBit`    | `Boolean`               | Sets or clears the bit at an offset, returns the old bit |
| `Redis#bitCount`  | `Long`                  | Counts bits set to 1, optionally within a `Range`      |
| `Redis#bitPos`    | `Long`                  | Finds the first set or cleared bit, optionally in a `BitPosRange` |
| `Redis#bitOp`     | `Long`                  | Applies a `BitOperation` to source keys and stores the result |
| `Redis#bitField`  | `Chunk[Option[Long]]`   | Runs one or more `BitFieldCommand` values              |

`BitOperation` has the cases `AND`, `OR`, `XOR` and `NOT`. `BitPosRange(start, end)` takes a start offset and an optional end offset.

To track daily visits per user and combine two days:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def visits(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  for {
    _     <- redis.setBit("visits:mon", 7L, value = true)
    _     <- redis.setBit("visits:tue", 7L, value = true)
    _     <- redis.bitOp(BitOperation.AND, "visits:both", "visits:mon", "visits:tue")
    count <- redis.bitCount("visits:both")
  } yield count
```

`Redis#bitCount` accepts a Scala `Range`, and `Redis#bitPos` accepts a `BitPosRange`. To restrict both to the first bytes of a key:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def inFirstBytes(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, (Long, Long)] =
  for {
    ones  <- redis.bitCount("flags", Some(0 to 3))
    first <- redis.bitPos("flags", bit = true, Some(BitPosRange(0L, Some(3L))))
  } yield (ones, first)
```

#### Bit Fields

`Redis#bitField` treats a string as a sequence of integers of any width. It takes one `BitFieldCommand` and any number of further ones, and returns one `Option[Long]` per command:

| Type                           | Fields                                  | Description                                  |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `BitFieldCommand.BitFieldGet`  | `type`, `offset`                        | Reads an integer                             |
| `BitFieldCommand.BitFieldSet`  | `type`, `offset`, `value`               | Writes an integer                            |
| `BitFieldCommand.BitFieldIncr` | `type`, `offset`, `increment`           | Adds to an integer                           |
| `BitFieldCommand.BitFieldOverflow` | `Fail`, `Sat`, `Wrap`               | Selects overflow behavior for later commands |

The integer type is a `BitFieldType`, either `BitFieldType.UnsignedInt(size)` or `BitFieldType.SignedInt(size)`. To write and increment an unsigned 8-bit counter with saturating overflow:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._
import zio.redis.BitFieldCommand._

def bitFields(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Chunk[Option[Long]]] =
  redis.bitField(
    "counters",
    BitFieldSet(BitFieldType.UnsignedInt(8), 0, 250L),
    BitFieldOverflow.Sat,
    BitFieldIncr(BitFieldType.UnsignedInt(8), 0, 10L)
  )
```

### Longest Common Subsequence

`Redis#lcs` compares the values of two keys. It takes an optional `LcsQueryType` and returns an `Lcs`:

| `LcsQueryType`                                | Result                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| none                                          | `Lcs.PlainLcs(lcs)` with the common subsequence     |
| `LcsQueryType.Len`                            | `Lcs.Length(length)` with its length                |
| `LcsQueryType.Idx(minMatchLength, withMatchLength)` | `Lcs.Matches(matches, length)` with match ranges |

Each `Match` holds two `MatchIdx(start, end)` ranges and, when `withMatchLength` is set, a `matchLength`. `minMatchLength` defaults to `1` and `withMatchLength` to `false`. To print the length of the shared text:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def commonLength(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Long] =
  redis.lcs("key1", "key2", Some(LcsQueryType.Len)).map {
    case Lcs.Length(length)   => length
    case Lcs.PlainLcs(lcs)    => lcs.length.toLong
    case Lcs.Matches(_, size) => size
  }
```

---

## Configuration(Reference)

`Redis.singleNode` connects to the server described by a `RedisConfig`; `Redis.local` uses `RedisConfig.Local`. This page lists every setting and shows how to supply it.

### RedisConfig

`RedisConfig` is a case class with the following fields:

| Field               | Type                       | Default                | Meaning                                              |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`              | `String`                   | none                   | Server host name                                     |
| `port`              | `Int`                      | none                   | Server port                                          |
| `sni`               | `Option[String]`           | `None`                 | Server name sent during the TLS handshake            |
| `ssl`               | `Boolean`                  | `false`                | Whether to connect over TLS                          |
| `verifyCertificate` | `Boolean`                  | `true`                 | Whether to verify the server certificate             |
| `requestQueueSize`  | `Int`                      | `16`                   | Size of the queue of requests waiting to be sent     |
| `auth`              | `Option[RedisConfig.Auth]` | `None`                 | Credentials, sent when the connection opens          |

`RedisConfig.Local` is `RedisConfig("localhost", 6379)`.

### Connecting to a Server

To connect to a named host and supply the config as a layer:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

val config: ULayer[RedisConfig] =
  ZLayer.succeed(RedisConfig("redis.example.com", 6379))

val redis: ZLayer[Any, RedisError.IOError, Redis] =
  ZLayer.make[Redis](
    config,
    ZLayer.succeed[CodecSupplier](CodecSupplier.utf8),
    Redis.singleNode
  )
```

### Authentication and TLS

To authenticate with a password, set `auth` to a `RedisConfig.Auth`. Add a `username` when the server uses ACL users. To use TLS, set `ssl = true`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

val secure: RedisConfig =
  RedisConfig(
    host = "redis.example.com",
    port = 6380,
    ssl = true,
    auth = Some(RedisConfig.Auth("secret", Some("app-user")))
  )
```

Set `verifyCertificate = false` only for development servers with self-signed certificates.

### RedisUri

`RedisUri` identifies a node by host and port. It is used by `RedisClusterConfig` to list cluster addresses, and it renders as `redis://host:port` (or `rediss://` when TLS is on). The companion offers several `apply` overloads:

```scala
import zio.redis._

val plain  = RedisUri("localhost", 6379)
val parsed = RedisUri("localhost:6379")
val tls    = RedisUri("redis.example.com:6380", ssl = true)
```

`RedisUri.apply` with a `"host:port"` string splits on `:`, so it does not accept IPv6 literals or full `redis://` URLs.

## EmbeddedRedis

`EmbeddedRedis` is the entry point of the `zio-redis-embedded` module. It starts a real Redis server as a child process and exposes its address as a `RedisConfig`. Add the module as shown in [Modules](../index.md#modules). For a worked spec, see [How to Test With Embedded Redis](../how-to/test-with-embedded-redis.md).

### layer

`EmbeddedRedis.layer` has the type:

```scala
lazy val layer: ZLayer[Any, Throwable, RedisConfig]
```

Building the layer finds a free TCP port, starts a Redis server on it and produces `RedisConfig("localhost", port)`. Closing the layer's scope stops the server. Because the output is a `RedisConfig`, it feeds [`Redis.singleNode`](./redis.md#layers) and `RedisSubscription.singleNode` directly. For a worked wiring, see [How to Test With Embedded Redis](../how-to/test-with-embedded-redis.md).

The layer fails with the `Throwable` raised when the server cannot be started, for example when the Redis binary cannot be launched.

### Limits

The server is a single node, started with the default configuration of the bundled `embedded-redis` library. Its Redis version is whatever that library ships.

## Redis

`Redis` is the service that exposes every Redis command except the subscription commands. `AsyncRedis` is the same service in pipelined form. Both are produced by the layers on this page, and both finish commands that return a value with a result builder.

### Services

Both services are aliases for `GenRedis`, which differs only in what each command returns:

```scala
type Redis      = GenRedis[GenRedis.Sync]
type AsyncRedis = GenRedis[GenRedis.Async]
```

A command on `Redis` returns `IO[RedisError, A]`. The same command on `AsyncRedis` returns `UIO[IO[RedisError, A]]`; see [AsyncRedis](../concepts/async-redis.md). Subscription commands live on a separate service, `RedisSubscription`; see [Pub/Sub](../concepts/pub-sub.md).

### Layers

`Redis.local` connects to `localhost:6379`. It needs a `CodecSupplier` and provides both services:

```scala
lazy val local: ZLayer[CodecSupplier, RedisError.IOError, Redis & AsyncRedis]
```

`Redis.singleNode` connects to the server described by a [`RedisConfig`](./configuration.md#redisconfig). It provides both services:

```scala
lazy val singleNode: ZLayer[CodecSupplier & RedisConfig, RedisError.IOError, Redis & AsyncRedis]
```

`Redis.cluster` connects to a Redis Cluster described by a `RedisClusterConfig`. It provides only `Redis`, and its error type is the general `RedisError`; see [Cluster](../concepts/cluster.md):

```scala
lazy val cluster: ZLayer[CodecSupplier & RedisClusterConfig, RedisError, Redis]
```

Every layer opens its connection when it is built and closes it when its scope ends. All three need a `CodecSupplier`; see [Codecs](../concepts/codecs.md).

### Result Builders

Redis stores bytes, so commands that return user data cannot know which type to decode to. They return a result builder, and the call is finished with `returning`. The number of type parameters depends on the shape of the reply:

| Builder                | Method                                  | Used by commands returning        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `ResultBuilder1`       | `returning[R: Schema]`                  | one value type, such as `Option[R]` or `Chunk[R]` |
| `ResultBuilder2`       | `returning[R1: Schema, R2: Schema]`     | two value types, such as `Map[R1, R2]` |
| `ResultBuilder3`       | `returning[R1: Schema, R2: Schema, R3: Schema]` | three value types, as in stream entries |
| `ResultOutputBuilder`  | `returning[R: Output]`                  | script results, decoded with an `Output` |
| `ResultStreamBuilder1` | `returning[R: Schema]`                  | a `Stream[RedisError, ...]`, as in subscriptions |

For example, `get` returns a `ResultBuilder1[Option, G]`, so its result type is chosen at the call site:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

def readName(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Option[String]] =
  redis.get("name").returning[String]

def readProfile(redis: Redis): IO[RedisError, Map[String, String]] =
  redis.hGetAll("profile").returning[String, String]
```

A builder cannot be used as an effect. Its `map` and `flatMap` require an implicit `NeedsReturnType`, which is never available, so forgetting `returning` is a compile error that reads "Use `returning[A]` to specify method's return type".

## Tutorial: Build a Rate Limiter

Welcome! In this tutorial we build a small rate limiter with ZIO Redis. By the end, you will have a service that allows at most a fixed number of requests per client in each time window, backed by a Redis counter that expires on its own.

We assume a Redis server on `localhost:6379` and the dependency from [Getting Started](../getting-started.md).

### How It Works

The limiter uses one counter per client and window. Each request increments the counter. The first request in a window also gives the counter an expiry equal to the window length, so Redis deletes it when the window ends. A request is allowed while the counter is at most the limit:

```
request ──> INCR rate:alice ──> count == 1? ──yes──> EXPIRE rate:alice window
                │
                └──> count <= limit ? allow : reject
```

### Step 1: Describe the Limiter

To keep the limiter independent of Redis, we start with a small service interface:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

trait RateLimiter {
  def allow(clientId: String): IO[RedisError, Boolean]
}
```

### Step 2: Implement It With INCR and EXPIRE

`Redis#incr` creates the key with value `1` when it is missing and returns the new count. When the count is `1`, we set the expiry with `Redis#expire`:

```scala
final case class RedisRateLimiter(redis: Redis, limit: Long, window: Duration) extends RateLimiter {
  def allow(clientId: String): IO[RedisError, Boolean] = {
    val key = s"rate:$clientId"

    for {
      count <- redis.incr(key)
      _     <- redis.expire(key, window).when(count == 1L)
    } yield count <= limit
  }
}
```

### Step 3: Provide a Layer

To make the limiter available to the rest of the program, we expose it as a layer:

```scala
object RateLimiter {
  def layer(limit: Long, window: Duration): URLayer[Redis, RateLimiter] =
    ZLayer.fromFunction((redis: Redis) => RedisRateLimiter(redis, limit, window): RateLimiter)
}
```

### Step 4: Use It

To run the limiter, we provide the `Redis` layer from [Getting Started](../getting-started.md) and call `RateLimiter#allow` repeatedly. With a limit of 3 per 10 seconds, the fourth call is rejected:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.redis._

object RateLimiterApp extends ZIOAppDefault {
  val program: ZIO[RateLimiter, RedisError, Unit] =
    ZIO.foreachDiscard(1 to 5) { i =>
      ZIO.serviceWithZIO[RateLimiter](_.allow("alice")).flatMap { ok =>
        ZIO.debug(s"request $i allowed: $ok")
      }
    }

  def run =
    program.provide(
      RateLimiter.layer(limit = 3, window = 10.seconds),
      Redis.local,
      ZLayer.succeed[CodecSupplier](CodecSupplier.utf8)
    )
}
```

### A Known Weakness

If the process fails between `Redis#incr` and `Redis#expire` on the first request, the counter never expires and the client stays blocked. To close that gap, move both steps into one Lua script; see [Scripting](../reference/commands/scripting.md).

### Next Steps

- [How to Cache Values With a Time to Live](../how-to/cache-with-ttl.md)
- [How to Build a Distributed Lock](../how-to/distributed-lock.md)
