## Getting Started with ZIO SBT

This page takes an sbt project from nothing to a formatted, linted build with a generated CI workflow. Each step uses one of the plugins listed in the [introduction](./index.md).

### Prerequisites

We need an sbt build with a `project/build.properties` file that names a current sbt version. The installation steps are in [Installation](./index.md#installation).

### Step 1: Add the Plugins

To add the plugins, put these lines in `project/plugins.sbt`:

```scala
addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ecosystem" % "0.8.12")

addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ci"        % "0.8.12")

addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-website"   % "0.8.12")

resolvers ++= Resolver.sonatypeOssRepos("public")
```

The `resolvers` line is only needed to use SNAPSHOT versions of the plugins.

### Step 2: Configure the Build

To apply the standard ZIO settings, set the ZIO version explicitly and call `stdSettings` in the build:

```scala
ThisBuild / zioVersion := "2.1.22"

lazy val root = project
  .in(file("."))
  .settings(stdSettings(name = Some("my-library")))
  .settings(enableZIO())
```

`zioVersion` has a default, but the default changes with every release of `zio-sbt-ecosystem`, so set it explicitly. The other settings are described in the [ZIO SBT Ecosystem reference](./reference/ecosystem.md).

### Step 3: Format and Lint

The ecosystem plugin adds the `fmt`, `lint` and `prepare` commands. To format all sources and apply scalafix rules before a pull request:

```bash
sbt prepare
```

To check that formatting and scalafix are clean, the same way CI does:

```bash
sbt lint
```

### Step 4: Generate the CI Workflow

The CI plugin generates `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the other workflow files from `build.sbt`:

```bash
sbt ciGenerateGithubWorkflow
```

Commit the generated files and never edit them by hand. The [ZIO SBT CI reference](./reference/ci.md) lists the generated files, the default jobs and every setting that changes them.

:::note
To use the CI plugin, install the [ZIO Assistant](https://github.com/apps/zio-assistant) GitHub App on the repository.
:::

### Step 5: Build the Documentation

The website plugin compiles the documentation in `docs/` and scaffolds the Docusaurus website. To compile the docs, then create the website the first time:

```bash
sbt docs/compileDocs
sbt docs/installWebsite
```

To preview the website on `http://localhost:3000`:

```bash
sbt docs/previewWebsite
```

The compiled output goes to `website/docs`, which is generated and must stay out of version control. The [ZIO SBT Website reference](./reference/website.md) shows the `.gitignore` entries.

### Next Steps

To see the whole path with a worked project, follow the [tutorial](./tutorials/set-up-a-new-zio-library.md). To solve a specific problem, pick a guide from the How-to Guides section.

---

## Add a Service Container to a Job

Jobs that need a database can attach a service. `options` carries the raw `docker create` arguments, which is where the health check goes — without one the job races the container and steps can start before it accepts connections:

```scala
import zio.Chunk
import zio.sbt.githubactions.{ImageRef, Service, ServicePort}

Job(
  id = "test",
  name = "Test",
  services = Seq(
    Service(
      name = "postgres",
      image = ImageRef("postgres:16"),
      env = Map("POSTGRES_USER" -> "postgres", "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" -> "postgres"),
      ports = Chunk(ServicePort(5432, 5432)),
      options = Some("--health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5")
    )
  ),
  steps = ...
)
```

`ServicePort(inner, outer)` renders as `inner:outer`, which GitHub reads as `<host>:<container>` — so `inner` is the port a step connects to on `localhost`.

---

## Auto-Approve and Auto-Merge Dependency Update PRs

Besides `ci.yml`, the `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` task also generates two more workflow files: `auto-approve.yml` and `auto-merge.yml`. These workflows automatically approve, and squash-merge once CI is green, pull requests opened by dependency-update bots, such as [Scala Steward](https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward), [Dependabot](https://github.com/dependabot), and [Renovate](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate).

Both workflows trigger on `pull_request_target` and also support `workflow_dispatch`, which backfills the approval/auto-merge on every currently open PR from the configured bots—handy for recovering PRs that were opened before the workflow existed, or after a workflow bug is fixed.

The set of trusted bots is controlled by the `ciDependencyUpdateBots` setting, which takes a `Seq[DependencyBot]`:

```scala
import zio.sbt.githubactions.DependencyBot

ciDependencyUpdateBots := Seq(
  DependencyBot.Dependabot,
  DependencyBot.Renovate,
  DependencyBot.ScalaSteward("zio-scala-steward"),
  DependencyBot.Custom("some-other-bot[bot]")
)
```

- `DependencyBot.Dependabot` — matches login `dependabot[bot]`
- `DependencyBot.Renovate` — matches login `renovate[bot]`
- `DependencyBot.ScalaSteward(githubAppName)` — matches login `<githubAppName>[bot]`, where `githubAppName` is the name of the GitHub App you registered for Scala Steward
- `DependencyBot.Custom(login)` — matches any exact GitHub login, for bots not covered by the predefined cases

The default value mirrors the bots used by the `zio/zio` repository: `Seq(DependencyBot.Dependabot, DependencyBot.Renovate, DependencyBot.ScalaSteward("zio-scala-steward"))`. If your Scala Steward GitHub App has a different name, override the setting with the correct `ScalaSteward` app name.

> **Note:**
>
> When the PR's base branch requires status checks (through classic branch protection or a ruleset), `auto-merge.yml` enables GitHub's native auto-merge with `gh pr merge --auto --squash` and finishes at once; GitHub merges the PR when the required checks pass. On a branch without required status checks, where `--auto` would merge before CI finishes, it instead waits for every check on the PR (other than its own bot jobs) to finish and merges with `gh pr merge --squash` only if none failed. A red check fails the job and leaves the PR open. The `workflow_dispatch` backfill still uses `gh pr merge --auto`, which merges immediately on a branch with no required status checks, so configure branch protection with required checks before relying on it.

> **Note:**
>
> `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never be granted the "workflows" scope needed to auto-merge a bot PR that touches `.github/workflows/**`, so `auto-merge.yml` mints a GitHub App token for that case instead, falling back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` when no app is configured (which still auto-merges ordinary, non-workflow-touching PRs fine). This needs the same `APP_ID`/`APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets as `update-readme`, and the [ZIO Assistant](https://github.com/apps/zio-assistant) app installation must additionally have the **Workflows** repository permission granted and accepted — without it, workflow-touching PRs still fail to auto-merge and need a manual merge.

---

## Build a Workflow of Only Custom Jobs

A build that replaces every stock job, for instance one whose jobs are generated from its module list, can also drop the two things the plugin adds around them: the aggregate `ci` job, and the workflow-level `permissions` block.

```scala
ciReportSuccessfulJobs := Seq.empty // no aggregate `ci` job
ciWorkflowPermissions  := None      // inherit the repository's default token permissions
ciConcurrency          := None
ciWorkflowEnv          := Map.empty
```

Omit `permissions` when a job needs more than the default `contents: read`, such as one that pushes a release tag with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. `None` is not the same as `Some(Map.empty)`, which renders `permissions: {}` and grants the token nothing.

---

## Change the Workflow Environment

By default the workflow exports `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`, built from `ciJvmOptions`. That is not always wanted: it makes `java -version` print a note containing commas, which corrupts the cache keys computed by `setup-sbt` and `coursier/cache-action`. Assigning `ciWorkflowEnv` replaces the derived map, so JVM flags can go through `SBT_OPTS` instead:

```scala
ciWorkflowEnv := Map(
  "SBT_OPTS" -> "-XX:+PrintCommandLineFlags -Djava.locale.providers=CLDR,JRE"
)
```

---

## Configure Dependabot Updates

`ciEnableDependabot` defaults to `true`, so `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` also generates `.github/dependabot.yml` from `ciDependabotConfig`. The default is a single weekly `github-actions` update at the repository root, which is what the ZIO-ecosystem repos use. Add more ecosystems, directories, intervals or groups explicitly; nothing is auto-detected:

```scala
import zio.sbt.githubactions.{DependabotConfig, DependabotGroup, DependabotUpdate}

ThisBuild / ciDependabotConfig := DependabotConfig(
  Seq(
    DependabotUpdate("github-actions"),
    DependabotUpdate(
      "npm",
      directory = "/website",
      openPullRequestsLimit = Some(5),
      groups = Seq(DependabotGroup("docusaurus", patterns = Seq("@docusaurus/*", "react")))
    )
  )
)
```

Unlike `.scala-steward.conf`, the file is fully owned by the plugin: a hand-written `dependabot.yml` is **overwritten** on the next `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow`, and `ciCheckGithubWorkflow` fails if it differs from the generated one. Set `ciEnableDependabot := false` to opt out; the plugin then deletes only a `dependabot.yml` carrying its "autogenerated" header, never a hand-written one.

---

## Configure Scala Steward

`ciEnableScalaSteward` defaults to `true`, so `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` generates `scala-steward.yml` automatically, which runs [`scala-steward-org/scala-steward-action`](https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward-action) on a daily schedule (`ciScalaStewardSchedule`, default `"0 0 * * *"`) to open dependency-update pull requests, authenticating as a GitHub App via the `SCALA_STEWARD_GITHUB_APP_ID`, `SCALA_STEWARD_GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` and `SCALA_STEWARD_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` repository secrets. Set it to `false` to opt out:

```scala
ThisBuild / ciEnableScalaSteward := false
```

`ciScalaStewardTimeoutMinutes` (default `45`), `ciScalaStewardPermissions` (default `contents: read` — the action authenticates via the GitHub App's installation token, since `github-app-auth-only` is always set, so no write scope is needed by default) and `ciScalaStewardWorkflowEnv` (default empty; a repo needing JVM tuning during dependency resolution sets `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`/similar here) all override the generated job.

The first time this feature renders a non-empty `.scala-steward.conf` from `ciScalaStewardConfig`, it scaffolds that file at the repository root, if it does not already exist. Like `.github/release-drafter.yml`, it is **never rewritten or deleted afterward**, even if `ciScalaStewardConfig` changes or `ciEnableScalaSteward` is turned back off — repo-specific pins/ignores/grouping are meant to be hand-customized once scaffolded, and `ciCheckGithubWorkflow`'s drift check does not cover it either, only `.github/workflows/scala-steward.yml` does. An all-default `ciScalaStewardConfig` renders to nothing, so most repos never see this file at all unless they set it.

This is purely additive: it does not change `ci.yml`'s own triggers or jobs. Because the feature defaults to *on*, a repo that already hand-maintains a `scala-steward.yml` (as every ZIO-ecosystem repo currently does) has that file **overwritten** by the generated workflow the next time `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` runs, exactly like `ci.yml` — silently, with no warning — and `ciCheckGithubWorkflow` fails until the regenerated file is committed. The hand-edited `.scala-steward.conf` is unaffected. To keep a hand-written workflow, set `ciEnableScalaSteward := false`: when disabled, the plugin only deletes a `scala-steward.yml` it generated itself — identified by its "autogenerated" header — and never a hand-written one. To customize the generated workflow instead, use `ciScalaStewardSchedule`, `ciScalaStewardTimeoutMinutes`, `ciScalaStewardPermissions`, `ciScalaStewardWorkflowEnv` and `ciScalaStewardConfig`.

---

## Control CI Concurrency

By default one run per branch is kept and in-progress runs are cancelled. `cancelInProgress` accepts an expression as well as a boolean, which is what lets a workflow cancel superseded pull request runs while letting releases finish:

```scala
import zio.sbt.githubactions.{CancelInProgress, Concurrency, Condition}

ciConcurrency := Some(
  Concurrency(
    group = "ci-pr-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}",
    cancelInProgress = CancelInProgress.When(Condition.Expression("github.event_name == 'pull_request'"))
  )
)
```

Individual jobs can override it. A release should generally not be cancelled halfway through:

```scala
Job(
  id = "release",
  name = "Release",
  concurrency = Some(
    Concurrency(group = "release-${{ github.ref }}", cancelInProgress = CancelInProgress.Never)
  ),
  steps = ...
)
```

---

## Customize the Generated CI Jobs

Jobs are values, so they can be transformed or replaced. The types live in `zio.sbt.githubactions` and the reusable steps in `zio.sbt.ZioSbtCiPlugin`; neither is exported through `autoImport`, so import them explicitly.

To adjust the generated jobs, map over them:

```scala
import zio.sbt.githubactions.Job

def onUbuntu22(job: Job): Job = job.copy(runsOn = "ubuntu-22.04")

inThisBuild(
  List(
    ciTestJobs  := ciTestJobs.value.map(onUbuntu22),
    ciBuildJobs := ciBuildJobs.value.map(onUbuntu22)
  )
)
```

To write one from scratch, build it from the exported steps:

```scala
import zio.sbt.ZioSbtCiPlugin._
import zio.sbt.githubactions.{Job, Step, Strategy}

ciTestJobs := Seq(
  Job(
    id = "integration-test",
    name = "Integration Test",
    jobTimeout = Some(30),
    strategy = Some(Strategy(matrix = Map("java" -> List("17", "21")), failFast = false)),
    steps = Seq(
      Checkout.value,
      SetupJava("17"),
      SetupSBT,
      CacheDependencies,
      Step.SingleStep(name = "Test", run = Some("sbt it:test"))
    )
  )
)
```

The aggregate `ci` job waits on the ids of whatever `ciLintJobs`, `ciTestJobs` and `ciBuildJobs`
produce, so replacing `test` with `integration-test` above is enough on its own. Set
`ciPullRequestApprovalJobs` only to wait on a different set than those three:

```scala
ciPullRequestApprovalJobs := Seq("lint", "integration-test")
```

`Checkout`, `SetupJava(version)`, `SetupSBT`, `CacheDependencies`, `SetupNodeJs` and `SetSwapSpace` are all available; the ones defined as settings need `.value`. (`SetupLibuv` is deprecated and no longer used by the generated jobs; Scala Native does not need libuv, so drop it from custom jobs.)

---

## Customize the Generated README

The `README.md` of a project is generated by `sbt docs/generateReadme` from the introduction in `docs/index.md` and a set of `readme*` settings, so edit those instead of the file. This guide shows how to change a section and how to keep the README up to date.

To replace the title with a banner, set `readmeBanner`. When a banner is set, the `# <projectName>` title is left out unless `readmeShowTitle` says otherwise:

```scala
readmeBanner := "<p align=\"center\"><img src=\"logo.png\" /></p>"
```

To add to a default section instead of replacing it, append to its current value:

```scala
readmeContribution := readmeContribution.value + "\n\nRun `sbt prepare` before you submit a pull request."
```

To fill a section that is empty by default, such as the maintainers, assign a Markdown string:

```scala
readmeMaintainers := "- [A Maintainer](https://github.com/a-maintainer)"
```

An empty string for `readmeAcknowledgement`, `readmeCredits` or `readmeMaintainers` leaves the section out.

To regenerate the README after a change:

```bash
sbt docs/generateReadme
```

To fail a build when the committed README is out of date, run `sbt docs/checkReadme`. The generated CI workflow regenerates the README with the `update-readme` job, which is described in [ZIO SBT CI](../reference/ci.md#default-jobs).

The list of settings and their defaults is in the [ZIO SBT Website reference](../reference/website.md#readme-settings).

---

## Draft Releases with Release Drafter

`ciEnableReleaseDrafter` defaults to `true`, so `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` generates `release-drafter.yml` automatically, which runs [`release-drafter/release-drafter`](https://github.com/release-drafter/release-drafter) on every push to the release branch to keep a draft GitHub Release up to date with categorized notes for each merged pull request. Set it to `false` to opt out:

```scala
ThisBuild / ciEnableReleaseDrafter := false
```

The first time the feature generates a `release-drafter.yml`, `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` also scaffolds `.github/release-drafter.yml` — release-drafter's own config file — from `ciReleaseDrafterCategories`/`ciReleaseDrafterExcludeLabels`/`ciReleaseDrafterAutolabeler`/`ciReleaseDrafterVersionResolver`, if that file doesn't already exist. Unlike every other generated file, it is **never rewritten or deleted afterward**, even if those settings change or `ciEnableReleaseDrafter` is turned back off: category/label taxonomy is inherently per-repo and meant to be hand-customized once scaffolded, so `ciCheckGithubWorkflow`'s drift check does not cover it either — only `.github/workflows/release-drafter.yml` (the workflow file) participates in that check, the same as `ci.yml`/`auto-approve.yml`/`auto-merge.yml`/`deploy-preview.yml`.

`release-drafter.yml`'s `push` trigger runs on `ciReleaseDrafterBranch` when set, otherwise the first entry of `ciEnabledBranches`, otherwise `main` — GitHub Actions' static `on.push.branches` list can't use the same `default_branch` runtime expression this plugin uses elsewhere, so a literal branch name is always required. Repos maintaining multiple release series (e.g. `series/2.x`) should set `ciReleaseDrafterBranch` explicitly.

This is purely additive: it does not change `ci.yml`'s own triggers or jobs, and it does not publish the draft release automatically — a human still does that, which is what fires the existing `release: published`-gated release jobs. Because the feature defaults to *on*, a repo that already hand-maintains a `release-drafter.yml` (release-drafter's own README convention) has that file **overwritten** by the generated workflow the next time `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` runs, exactly like `ci.yml` — silently, with no warning, so custom triggers, `runs-on` or steps are lost. `ciCheckGithubWorkflow` fails until the regenerated file is committed. The hand-edited `.github/release-drafter.yml` config file is unaffected. To keep a hand-written workflow, set `ciEnableReleaseDrafter := false`: when disabled, the plugin only deletes a `release-drafter.yml` it generated itself — identified by the "autogenerated" header every generated workflow carries — and never a hand-written one. To customize the generated workflow instead, use `ciReleaseDrafterBranch`, `ciReleaseDrafterCategories`, `ciReleaseDrafterExcludeLabels`, `ciReleaseDrafterAutolabeler` and `ciReleaseDrafterVersionResolver`.

---

## Enable Netlify Deploy Previews

Setting `ciEnableDeployPreview := true` makes `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` also generate `deploy-preview.yml`, which deploys the built Docusaurus site to Netlify for every pull request that touches `docs/` or `website/`.

```scala
ThisBuild / ciEnableDeployPreview := true
```

The feature is split across two workflows, decoupled by artifacts rather than triggering the deploy directly from a pull request event:

- The `build` job gains a few extra steps. `Check website is installed` runs first, checking that `website/package.json` and `website/docusaurus.config.js` both exist — the same signal [`installWebsite`](../reference/website.md) itself uses to tell a real Docusaurus scaffold apart from a `website/` directory holding only `mdocOut`'s generated output. Only when the website is installed does the job go on to detect whether the pull request touched `docs/` or `website/`, and if so upload `website/build` as a `website-artifact`, plus the PR number as a `pr-metadata` artifact.
- `deploy-preview.yml` triggers on `workflow_run` once the CI workflow completes, downloads those two artifacts, deploys `website-artifact` to Netlify with [`nwtgck/actions-netlify`](https://github.com/nwtgck/actions-netlify) under a deterministic `pr-<number>` alias — so the preview URL for a given PR is stable across redeploys, of the shape `pr-<number>--<your-netlify-site-name>.netlify.app` — then posts a fresh comment with the preview URL via [`peter-evans/create-or-update-comment`](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-or-update-comment) — each deploy gets its own comment rather than editing one in place, so pushing a follow-up commit doesn't erase the record of the previous deploy. Earlier preview comments (tagged with an `<!-- netlify-preview-comment -->` marker) are collapsed as outdated first, via [`actions/github-script`](https://github.com/actions/github-script), so the thread doesn't accumulate clutter — the whole comment history is paginated through, not just the first page, so this still works on pull requests with a long comment history.

Using `workflow_run` instead of triggering directly on `pull_request` means the deploy step only ever runs after CI has actually succeeded, and it runs with read/write access to secrets even for pull requests from forks (where a plain `pull_request` trigger would not have that access).

`deploy-preview.yml` triggers on *every* successful pull-request CI run, not only the ones where `build` actually uploaded artifacts — a PR that doesn't touch `docs/`/`website/`, or a repo with no website installed yet, never produces `website-artifact`/`pr-metadata` at all. To handle that, the two `actions/download-artifact` steps set `continue-on-error: true`, since a missing artifact there is an expected outcome, not a failure worth stopping the job over; every step after them then checks `steps.download-website.outcome == 'success' && steps.download-pr-metadata.outcome == 'success'` before running. So a run with nothing to deploy ends with two soft-failed downloads and nothing else — no deploy call, no PR comment — instead of a hard job failure.

Put together, this makes `ciEnableDeployPreview` safe to turn on before the Docusaurus site exists: neither workflow does any real work until `website/` is a genuine installation and a pull request actually changes it.

This requires two repository secrets: `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`, a [personal access token](https://docs.netlify.com/api/get-started/#authentication) generated from the Netlify user account that owns the site, and `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`, found under the site's **Site configuration → General → Site details** in the Netlify dashboard. The default value of `ciEnableDeployPreview` is `false`, so existing builds see no change until they opt in.

##### On-demand previews

Every preview deploy costs Netlify credits. To deploy only when someone asks for it, switch the mode:

```scala
import zio.sbt.githubactions.DeployPreviewMode

ThisBuild / ciEnableDeployPreview := true
ThisBuild / ciDeployPreviewMode   := DeployPreviewMode.OnDemand
```

`ciDeployPreviewMode` defaults to `DeployPreviewMode.Automatic`, the behavior described above, so nothing changes until you opt in. With `OnDemand`, `deploy-preview.yml` is still generated, but it works differently:

1. After a successful pull-request CI run, the `post-preview-comment` job creates one bot comment on the pull request with an unticked **Deploy preview** checkbox. Nothing is deployed yet. A later push resets the same comment to the new commit with the box unticked again.
2. When someone ticks the box, GitHub fires an `issue_comment` `edited` event and the `deploy-preview` job runs. It first checks that the person who ticked has `admin`, `maintain` or `write` access to the repository and adds a 👍 reaction to the comment to acknowledge the request, then finds the successful `ci.yml` run for the exact commit named in the comment, downloads that run's `website-artifact`, and deploys it to Netlify.
3. The comment is rewritten with the preview URL, the deploy time and the commit, plus a **Redeploy preview** checkbox. If the deployment fails, the box is unticked again and the comment links to the failed run.

Deployments are serialized per pull request (a second tick waits for the first instead of cancelling it). The two Netlify secrets and the `website-artifact` / `pr-metadata` artifacts from `build` are the same as for the automatic mode, and the generated workflow looks up CI by its file name, `ci.yml`.

---

## Keep the Generated Workflow in Sync

The generated files are meant to be committed and never edited by hand. To stop them drifting from the build, run the check in CI — the default `lint` job already does:

```bash
sbt ciCheckGithubWorkflow
```

It regenerates the workflows and fails if the result differs from what is committed, naming the files that are stale. If a generated file is edited directly, the next run of this check fails, which is what keeps `build.sbt` the single source of truth.

---

## Publish a Release's Docs Again

`release-docs` needs `release`, and Maven Central rejects a version it already has. So when `release` has published a version but `release-docs` failed (for example, because the npm package was not set up yet), running `release` again fails with `already exists` and the docs are skipped again.

To publish the docs without the Maven release, run the CI workflow by hand with the `docs-only` input set to `true`:

```bash
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main -f docs-only=true
```

Or open **Actions → CI → Run workflow**, pick the branch, and type `true` in `docs-only`. The `release` job is skipped, `release-docs` publishes the docs, and `notify-docs-release` runs once they are published. The docs version is the newest `v*` tag in the repository; the docs content comes from the branch or tag the workflow runs on.

The run uses the `ci.yml` of that branch or tag, so the input is only there once the workflow has been regenerated with this version of the plugin. Every `workflow_dispatch` trigger of `ci.yml` gets the input, including one in a custom `ciWorkflowTriggers`, as long as the workflow has a `release-docs` job.

If the failure is caught right away, **Re-run failed jobs** on the original run also works: it keeps the successful `release` result and only runs `release-docs` and `notify-docs-release` again. **Re-run all jobs** runs `release` again and fails.

---

## Regenerate Workflows on Bot PRs

A bot PR often changes something the generated files depend on: Scala Steward bumping `zio-sbt-ci` itself, or Dependabot bumping an action pin in a generated workflow. Either leaves `ciCheckGithubWorkflow` failing in the Lint job, so the PR is red and `auto-merge.yml` never merges it, with nobody to fix it.

`ciEnableRegenerateWorkflows` defaults to `true`, so `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` also generates `regenerate-workflows.yml`. On every same-repository PR opened by one of `ciDependencyUpdateBots`, it checks out the PR branch, runs `sbt ciGenerateGithubWorkflow`, and, if anything under `.github` changed, commits and pushes the result to that branch. The push re-runs CI on the new commit and, since `auto-merge.yml` re-evaluates on every push, the PR then merges once CI is green.

Things to know:

- It pushes with the GitHub App token (`APP_ID`/`APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, the same as `auto-merge.yml`): a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger CI, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot push changes to `.github/workflows/**` at all. The App needs the **Workflows** repository permission.
- Workflows triggered by `dependabot[bot]` read the **Dependabot** secrets store, not the repository's Actions secrets. Add `APP_ID` and `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` under Settings → Secrets and variables → Dependabot.
- Regeneration is driven by your build, so a Dependabot bump of an action pin *in a generated workflow* is regenerated back to the plugin's own pin and the PR ends up empty. The plugin owns those pins; they move when `zio-sbt-ci` is bumped. If you rely on this, remove the `github-actions` ecosystem from `ciDependabotConfig`.
- Set `ciEnableRegenerateWorkflows := false` to opt out; the plugin then deletes only a `regenerate-workflows.yml` carrying its "autogenerated" header.

---

## Set Job Timeouts

A job with no timeout inherits GitHub's default of six hours, which is a long time to wait for a hung build:

```scala
Job(id = "test", name = "Test", jobTimeout = Some(25), steps = ...)

// or on an existing job
ciTestJobs := ciTestJobs.value.map(_.withTimeout(25))
```

> **Note:**
>
> `Job` also has an older `timeoutMinutes: Int` field. It predates `jobTimeout` and was accepted but never rendered, so it is deprecated. It is still honoured when set to anything other than its historical default of `30`, so builds that set it keep working.

---

## Test Against Several Scala and Java Versions

### Default Testing Strategy

The default testing strategy for ZIO SBT CI plugin is to run `sbt +test` on Corretto Java 17, 21 and 25. So this will generate the following job:

```yaml
test:
  name: Test
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  continue-on-error: false
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false
    matrix:
      java: ['17', '21', '25']
  steps:
  - name: Setup Scala
    uses: actions/setup-java@v5
    with:
      distribution: corretto
      java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
      check-latest: true
  - name: Cache Dependencies
    uses: coursier/cache-action@v6
  - name: Git Checkout
    uses: actions/checkout@v6
    with:
      fetch-depth: '0'
  - name: Test
    run: sbt --no-colors +test
```

The `sbt +test` command will run the `test` task for all submodules in the project against all Scala versions defined in the `crossScalaVersions` setting.

### Concurrent Testing Strategy

In some cases, we may have multiple submodules in our project and we want to test them concurrently using GitHub Actions matrix strategy.

The `ciTargetScalaVersions` setting key is used to define a mapping of project names to the Scala versions that should be used for testing phase of continuous integration (CI).

For example, suppose we have a project with the name "submoduleA" and we want to test it against Scala `2.12.20`, and for the "submoduleB" we want to test it against Scala `2.12.20` and `2.13.18` and `3.3.7`, We can define the `ciTargetScalaVersions` setting as follows:

```scala
ThisBuild / ciTargetScalaVersions := Map(
    "submoduleA" -> Seq("2.12.20"),
    "submoduleB" -> Seq("2.12.20", "2.13.18", "3.3.7")
  )
```

In the example provided, `ciTargetScalaVersions` is defined at the `ThisBuild` level, meaning that the setting will apply to all projects within the build. The setting defines a Map where the key is the name of the current project, obtained by calling the `id` method on the `thisProject` setting, and the value is a sequence of Scala versions obtained from the `crossScalaVersions` of each submodule setting.

To simplify this process, we can populate the versions using each submodule's crossScalaVersions setting as follows:

```scala
ThisBuild / ciTargetScalaVersions := Map(
  (submoduleA / thisProject).value.id -> (submoduleA / crossScalaVersions).value,
  (submoduleB / thisProject).value.id -> (submoduleB / crossScalaVersions).value
)
```

The above code can be simplified further by using `targetScalaVersionsFor` helper method, it takes a list of submodules and returns a Map of project names to their `crossScalaVersions`:

```scala
ThisBuild / ciTargetScalaVersions := targetScalaVersionsFor(submoduleA, submoduleB).value
```

This will generate the following job:

```yaml
test:
  name: Test
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  continue-on-error: false
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false
    matrix:
      java: ['17', '21', '25']
      scala-project:
      - ++2.12.20 submoduleA
      - ++2.12.20 submoduleB
      - ++2.13.18 submoduleB
      - ++3.3.7 submoduleB
  steps:
  - name: Setup Scala
    uses: actions/setup-java@v5
    with:
      distribution: corretto
      java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
      check-latest: true
  - name: Cache Dependencies
    uses: coursier/cache-action@v6
  - name: Git Checkout
    uses: actions/checkout@v6
    with:
      fetch-depth: '0'
  - name: Test
    run: sbt --no-colors ${{ matrix.scala-project }}/test
```

## Introduction to ZIO SBT

_ZIO SBT_ contains multiple sbt plugins that are useful for ZIO projects. It provides high-level SBT utilities that simplify the development of ZIO applications.

[![Production Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project%20Stage-Production%20Ready-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/zio/zio/wiki/Project-Stages) ![CI Badge](https://github.com/zio/zio-sbt/workflows/CI/badge.svg) [![Sonatype Releases](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/dev.zio/zio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0.svg?label=Sonatype%20Release)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/dev.zio/zio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0) [![Sonatype Snapshots](https://img.shields.io/maven-metadata/v?metadataUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fcentral.sonatype.com%2Frepository%2Fmaven-snapshots%2Fdev%2Fzio%2Fzio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0%2Fmaven-metadata.xml&label=Sonatype%20Snapshot)](https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/dev/zio/zio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0/) [![javadoc](https://javadoc.io/badge2/dev.zio/zio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0/javadoc.svg)](https://javadoc.io/doc/dev.zio/zio-sbt-website_2.12_1.0) [![ZIO SBT](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/zio/zio-sbt?style=social)](https://github.com/zio/zio-sbt)

### Overview

ZIO SBT is made of five modules, three of which are sbt plugins that a ZIO project enables in its build:

- **ZIO SBT Ecosystem** (`zio-sbt-ecosystem`) holds the standard settings, compiler options and commands (`fmt`, `lint`, `prepare`) that every ZIO project shares.
- **ZIO SBT Website** (`zio-sbt-website`) compiles the documentation in `docs/` with mdoc, builds and previews the Docusaurus website, publishes the docs to npm, and generates the `README.md`.
- **ZIO SBT CI** (`zio-sbt-ci`) generates the GitHub Actions workflows of a project from its `build.sbt`.
- **ZIO SBT GitHub Actions** (`zio-sbt-githubactions`) is the model of GitHub workflows (`Workflow`, `Job`, `Step`, ...) that ZIO SBT CI is built on. It comes with `zio-sbt-ci`, so it needs no installation of its own.
- **ZIO SBT Source** (`zio-sbt-source`) is a library, not an sbt plugin, that embeds source files and evaluated expressions into the documentation.

### Installation

Add the following lines to your `project/plugins.sbt` file:

```scala
// Standard settings, compiler options and the fmt, lint and prepare commands
addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ecosystem" % "0.8.12")

// Generates the GitHub Actions workflows from build.sbt
addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ci"        % "0.8.12")

// Builds, previews and publishes the documentation website
addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-website"   % "0.8.12")
```

Then you can enable them by using the following code in your `build.sbt` file:

```scala
enablePlugins(
  WebsitePlugin,
  ZioSbtEcosystemPlugin,
  ZioSbtCiPlugin
)
```

:::note
Always try to keep the SBT version specified in the `project/build.properties` file up to date to ensure compatibility with the ZIO SBT plugins.
:::

To embed source files into the documentation, also add `zio-sbt-source`, which is a regular library dependency and belongs in the `build.sbt` of the docs project:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-sbt-source" % "0.8.12"
```

### Where to Go Next

Read [Getting Started](https://zio.dev/zio-sbt/getting-started) to set up a project, the [Reference](https://zio.dev/zio-sbt/reference/) for every setting, task and command, and the [How-to Guides](https://zio.dev/zio-sbt/how-to-guides/publish-a-releases-docs-again) for common CI tasks.

---

## ZIO SBT CI

`ZioSbtCiPlugin` generates the GitHub Actions workflows of a project from its `build.sbt`, so continuous integration (CI) is configured in one place. The default workflow builds, tests, lints and publishes the project, and every part of it can be changed with sbt settings or replaced by custom jobs. The model of workflows, jobs and steps lives in [ZIO SBT GitHub Actions](./githubactions.md).

To install the plugin, add `addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ci" % "0.8.12")` to `project/plugins.sbt`, as described in [Installation](../index.md#installation). Using SNAPSHOT versions of the plugin also needs `resolvers ++= Resolver.sonatypeOssRepos("public")`.

The plugin declares `trigger = allRequirements`, so having it on the classpath is enough, and `enablePlugins(ZioSbtCiPlugin)` is not strictly required. Its settings are defined at `ThisBuild` level, so set them as `ThisBuild / ciSomething := ...`, or inside `inThisBuild(...)`.

To use the plugin, install the [ZIO Assistant](https://github.com/apps/zio-assistant) GitHub App on the repository.

### Generated Files

`ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` writes these files. Commit them and never edit them by hand. See [Keep the Generated Workflow in Sync](../how-to-guides/keep-the-workflow-in-sync.md) to check that they match the build.

| File                                       | Generated when                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml`                 | Always. The file name is `ciWorkflowTitle` lower-cased, with non-alphanumeric characters turned into `-` |
| `.github/workflows/auto-approve.yml`       | Always                                                                                      |
| `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`         | Always                                                                                      |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml`     | `ciEnableDeployPreview` is `true`                                                           |
| `.github/workflows/release-drafter.yml`    | `ciEnableReleaseDrafter` is `true` (the default). Scaffolds `.github/release-drafter.yml` once |
| `.github/workflows/scala-steward.yml`      | `ciEnableScalaSteward` is `true` (the default). Scaffolds `.scala-steward.conf` once when `ciScalaStewardConfig` renders content |
| `.github/dependabot.yml`                   | `ciEnableDependabot` is `true` (the default)                                                |
| `.github/workflows/regenerate-workflows.yml` | `ciEnableRegenerateWorkflows` is `true` (the default)                                     |

### Default Jobs

The generated `ci.yml` contains these jobs:

| Job | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `build` | Compiles everything, publishes locally, and builds the website |
| `lint` | Checks the generated workflow is up to date, then runs `sbt lint` |
| `test` | Runs the test suite across the target Java versions |
| `update-readme` | Regenerates `README.md` from `docs/index.md` and opens a PR |
| `ci` | Aggregate gate: succeeds only if the jobs above did. Point branch protection at this one |
| `release` | Runs `sbt ci-release` on a published release or a manual run, and on pushes to the default branch for SNAPSHOTs |
| `release-docs` | Publishes the docs to npm after a successful `release`, or on a manual run with `docs-only` set to `true` |
| `notify-docs-release` | Dispatches an `update-docs` event to `zio/zio` with the docs package name and version, so the ZIO website picks up the new docs |

`notify-docs-release` takes the docs version from the release tag, or from the newest `v` tag on a manual `docs-only` run, and waits for up to five minutes until npm lists exactly that version. It fails if the version never appears. With `HashVersioning` as `ciDocsVersioningScheme`, it still reads the `latest` version with `npm view <package> version`.

The default workflow runs on `workflow_dispatch`, published releases, pushes (to `ciEnabledBranches` when set, otherwise every branch) and pull requests that do not target `gh-pages`.

### Concurrency of the Default Workflow

By default `ciConcurrency` is one run per workflow and ref, and an in-progress run is cancelled when a newer run starts in the same group. The group is `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) && github.run_id || github.ref }}`. On the default branch the group ends with the run id, so every run is kept. On any other ref, including a tag such as `refs/tags/v1.9.2`, the group ends with the ref.

A release event and the push of its tag have the same ref, so they share one group, and the run that starts later cancels the earlier one. To change this, set `ciConcurrency` as described in [Control CI Concurrency](../how-to-guides/control-ci-concurrency.md).

### Settings

All settings are `ThisBuild`-scoped.

#### Workflow-Level

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ciWorkflowTitle` | `String` | `"CI"` | Workflow name. The file name is its lower-cased form with each run of non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-` (`ci.yml` for `CI`). Named this way to avoid colliding with zio-sbt-website's `ciWorkflowName`, which sets the README badge |
| `ciEnabledBranches` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq.empty` | Branches the workflow runs on. Empty means every branch |
| `ciWorkflowEnv` | `Map[String, String]` | derived from `ciJvmOptions`/`ciNodeOptions` | Workflow-level environment. Assigning **replaces** the derived map, which is how a build opts out of `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS` |
| `ciJvmOptions` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq.empty` | Appended to `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS` |
| `ciNodeOptions` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq.empty` | Sets `NODE_OPTIONS` when non-empty |
| `ciConcurrency` | `Option[Concurrency]` | one run per ref, cancelling in progress, except that every run on the default branch is kept | Concurrency group, or `None` to omit the block. See [Concurrency of the Default Workflow](#concurrency-of-the-default-workflow) |
| `ciWorkflowPermissions` | `Option[Map[String, String]]` | `Some(id-token: write, contents: read)` | Workflow-level `permissions`. `None` omits the block, so the workflow runs with the repository's default token permissions; `Some(Map.empty)` instead renders `permissions: {}`, which grants nothing |
| `ciSwapSizeGB` | `Int` | `0` | Adds a swap-space step to every job when greater than zero |
| `ciBackgroundJobs` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq.empty` | Commands prefixed to each `run`, for daemons a job needs |
| `ciEnableDeployPreview` | `Boolean` | `false` | Adds website-artifact upload steps to `build` and generates `deploy-preview.yml`. Requires `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NETLIFY_SITE_ID` secrets |
| `ciDeployPreviewMode` | `DeployPreviewMode` | `DeployPreviewMode.Automatic` | Only used with `ciEnableDeployPreview`. `Automatic` deploys every successful pull-request CI run; `OnDemand` posts a "Deploy preview" checkbox comment and deploys only when it is ticked |
| `ciEnableReleaseDrafter` | `Boolean` | `true` | Generates `release-drafter.yml` and scaffolds `.github/release-drafter.yml` (once). Overwrites a hand-written `release-drafter.yml` when on; when off, only deletes a copy it generated itself |
| `ciReleaseDrafterCategories` | `Seq[ReleaseDrafterCategory]` | Features/Bug Fixes/Maintenance/Dependency Updates | Categories written into the scaffolded config on first generation only |
| `ciReleaseDrafterVersionResolver` | `Option[ReleaseDrafterVersionResolver]` | `None` | Optional `version-resolver` block for the scaffolded config |
| `ciReleaseDrafterAutolabeler` | `Seq[ReleaseDrafterAutolabelerRule]` | `Seq.empty` | Optional `autolabeler` rules for the scaffolded config |
| `ciReleaseDrafterExcludeLabels` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq("skip-changelog")` | `exclude-labels` for the scaffolded config |
| `ciReleaseDrafterBranch` | `Option[Branch]` | `None` | Branch `release-drafter.yml`'s `push` trigger runs on. Falls back to the first of `ciEnabledBranches`, then `"main"` |
| `ciEnableScalaSteward` | `Boolean` | `true` | Generates `scala-steward.yml` and scaffolds `.scala-steward.conf` (once, only if non-empty). Overwrites a hand-written `scala-steward.yml` when on; when off, only deletes a copy it generated itself |
| `ciScalaStewardSchedule` | `String` | `"0 0 * * *"` | Cron schedule for `scala-steward.yml`'s `schedule` trigger |
| `ciScalaStewardTimeoutMinutes` | `Int` | `45` | `timeout-minutes` for the scala-steward job |
| `ciScalaStewardPermissions` | `Map[String, String]` | `contents: read` | Permissions block for `scala-steward.yml`; the action authenticates via the GitHub App's installation token, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so no write scope is needed by default |
| `ciScalaStewardWorkflowEnv` | `Map[String, String]` | `Map.empty` | Extra env vars for the scala-steward job |
| `ciScalaStewardConfig` | `ScalaStewardConfig` | `ScalaStewardConfig()` | Settings scaffolded into `.scala-steward.conf` on first non-empty render |
| `ciEnableDependabot` | `Boolean` | `true` | Generates `.github/dependabot.yml`. Overwrites a hand-written one when on; when off, only deletes a copy it generated itself |
| `ciEnableRegenerateWorkflows` | `Boolean` | `true` | Generates `regenerate-workflows.yml`, which re-runs `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` on bot PRs and pushes the result to the PR branch. When off, only deletes a copy it generated itself |
| `ciDependabotConfig` | `DependabotConfig` | one weekly `github-actions` update at `/` | Content of the generated `dependabot.yml` |

#### Test Matrix

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ciTargetJavaVersions` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq("17", "21", "25")` | Java versions in the test matrix |
| `ciDefaultJavaVersion` | `String` | `"17"` | Java version for the non-matrix jobs |
| `ciTargetScalaVersions` | `Map[String, Seq[String]]` | `Map.empty` | Module to Scala versions. Empty runs a plain `sbt +test` |
| `ciTargetMinJavaVersions` | `Map[String, String]` | `Map.empty` | Module to minimum Java version, gating modules per matrix entry |
| `ciGroupSimilarTests` | `Boolean` | `false` | Groups by Java and Scala version instead of one entry per module |
| `ciMatrixMaxParallel` | `Option[Int]` | `None` | `strategy.max-parallel` |

#### Jobs and Steps

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ciBuildJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | one `build` job | Replaces or extends the build jobs |
| `ciLintJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | one `lint` job | |
| `ciTestJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | one `test` job | |
| `ciUpdateReadmeJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | one `update-readme` job | Set to `Seq.empty` if the README is maintained by hand |
| `ciReportSuccessfulJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | the aggregate `ci` job | Set to `Seq.empty` for a workflow made up entirely of custom jobs that does not want one |
| `ciReleaseJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | one `release` job | |
| `ciPostReleaseJobs` | `Seq[Job]` | `release-docs`, `notify-docs-release` | |
| `ciPullRequestApprovalJobs` | `Seq[String]` | the ids of `ciLintJobs`, `ciTestJobs` and `ciBuildJobs` | Job ids the aggregate `ci` job waits on. Follows the jobs those three settings produce, so renaming or adding one is picked up without touching this |
| `ciReleaseApprovalJobs` | `Seq[String]` | `Seq("ci")` | Job ids the release waits on |
| `ciCheckArtifactsCompilationSteps` | `Seq[Step]` | `sbt +Test/compile` | |
| `ciCheckArtifactsBuildSteps` | `Seq[Step]` | `sbt +publishLocal` | |
| `ciCheckWebsiteBuildProcess` | `Seq[Step]` | `sbt docs/clean; sbt docs/buildWebsite`, then `sbt docs/checkDocsOnFreshWebsite` | Set to `Seq.empty` in a build with no `docs` project |
| `ciCheckGithubWorkflowSteps` | `Seq[Step]` | `sbt ciCheckGithubWorkflow` | |

#### Release and Docs

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ciPublishSnapshots` | `Boolean` | `true` | Also publish SNAPSHOTs on pushes to the default branch |
| `ciUpdateReadmeCondition` | `Option[Condition]` | `None` | When to run the README job. Defaults to published releases |
| `ciDocsVersioningScheme` | `DocsVersioning` | `SemanticVersioning` | `SemanticVersioning` or `HashVersioning` |
| `ciDependencyUpdateBots` | `Seq[DependencyBot]` | Dependabot, Renovate, `ScalaSteward("zio-scala-steward")` | Bots whose PRs are auto-approved and auto-merged |

#### Tasks

| Task | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` | Writes `ci.yml`, `auto-approve.yml` and `auto-merge.yml`, plus `deploy-preview.yml` when `ciEnableDeployPreview` is `true` and `release-drafter.yml` (and scaffolds `.github/release-drafter.yml` once) when `ciEnableReleaseDrafter` is `true`, and scala-steward.yml (and scaffolds .scala-steward.conf once, when ciScalaStewardConfig renders non-empty content) when ciEnableScalaSteward is true, `.github/dependabot.yml` when `ciEnableDependabot` is `true`, and `regenerate-workflows.yml` when `ciEnableRegenerateWorkflows` is `true` |
| `ciCheckGithubWorkflow` | Regenerates and fails if the committed files are stale |
| `ciGenerateAutoApproveWorkflow` | Writes `auto-approve.yml` only |
| `ciGenerateAutoMergeWorkflow` | Writes `auto-merge.yml` only |

### Types Used in Settings

The types that the settings above take, such as `Job`, `Step`, `Concurrency`, `DependencyBot` and `DeployPreviewMode`, are described in [ZIO SBT GitHub Actions](./githubactions.md). They live in `zio.sbt.githubactions` and are not exported through `autoImport`, so import them explicitly. The reusable steps live in `zio.sbt.ZioSbtCiPlugin`.

### Helper Methods

`targetScalaVersionsFor(projects*)` takes a list of projects and returns a `Map` from each project id to its `crossScalaVersions`. It is meant for `ciTargetScalaVersions`, as shown in [Test Against Several Scala and Java Versions](../how-to-guides/test-against-several-scala-and-java-versions.md).

## ZIO SBT Ecosystem

`ZioSbtEcosystemPlugin` provides the settings, tasks and commands that are common to every ZIO project. It is an auto plugin with `trigger = allRequirements`, so having it on the classpath enables it. It requires the sbt-header, sbt-scalafix, sbt-scalafmt and sbt-buildinfo plugins, which come with it.

To install it, add `addSbtPlugin("dev.zio" % "zio-sbt-ecosystem" % "0.8.12")` to `project/plugins.sbt`, as described in [Installation](../index.md#installation).

### Settings

The plugin defines these keys. The first seven are set at the `ThisBuild` level. `welcomeBannerEnabled` and `usefulTasksAndSettings` are set in each project.

| Setting                  | Type                  | Default                                  | Description                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scala212`               | `String`              | `"2.12.21"`                              | The Scala 2.12 version of the build                                                                               |
| `scala213`               | `String`              | `"2.13.18"`                              | The Scala 2.13 version of the build                                                                               |
| `scala3`                 | `String`              | `"3.9.0"`                                | The Scala 3 version of the build                                                                                  |
| `scalaVersion`           | `String`              | `scala213.value`                         | Set by the plugin, so a build compiles with Scala 2.13 unless it overrides this                                   |
| `crossScalaVersions`     | `Seq[String]`         | `Seq(scala212, scala213, scala3)`        | Set by the plugin                                                                                                 |
| `zioVersion`             | `String`              | `"2.1.22"`                               | The ZIO version that `enableZIO` adds as a dependency                                                             |
| `javaPlatform`           | `String`              | `"17"`                                   | The Java version passed to `-source` and `-target` and used for Scala compiler options                            |
| `welcomeBannerEnabled`   | `Boolean`             | `true`                                   | Whether sbt prints the welcome banner with the list of useful commands on startup                                 |
| `usefulTasksAndSettings` | `Map[String, String]` | the `lint`, `fmt`, `fix`, `prepare`, `quiet` and `publish-all` commands and the strict-compile tasks      | Name and description pairs that the welcome banner prints                                                         |

The defaults of `scala212`, `scala213`, `scala3` and `zioVersion` are baked into the version of the plugin, so upgrading the plugin changes them. Set `zioVersion` explicitly in every build:

```scala
ThisBuild / zioVersion := "2.1.22"
```

:::note
Don't rely on `zioVersion`'s default. It's baked into whichever version of zio-sbt-ecosystem you depend on, so upgrading the plugin—including via an automated dependency-update PR—can silently change your project's own ZIO version along with it. Setting `zioVersion` explicitly keeps that a deliberate decision you make, not a side effect of a plugin bump. Every ZIO ecosystem project (zio-logging, zio-kafka, zio-cache, and others) already follows this practice.
:::

The Scala version settings are plain `String` keys, so they can define `crossScalaVersions` or any other setting:

```scala
crossScalaVersions := Seq(scala212.value, scala213.value, scala3.value)
```

The plugin also sets these build-wide defaults: `organization := "dev.zio"`, the Apache 2 `licenses`, `homepage` and `scmInfo` derived from the lower-cased project name (`https://zio.dev/<name>` and `https://github.com/zio/<name>`), the `pgp*` keys for signing, and `onChangedBuildSource := ReloadOnSourceChanges`.

### Commands

The plugin registers these sbt commands. Each one except `quiet off` first turns the welcome banner off.

| Command       | What it runs                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fmt`         | `scalafmtSbt`, then `+scalafmt` and `+Test / scalafmt`: formats the sources                           |
| `lint`        | `enableStrictCompile`, the cross-built scalafmt checks, `scalafix --check`, then `disableStrictCompile` |
| `fix`         | `Compile / scalafix` and `Test / scalafix`: applies the scalafix rules                                |
| `prepare`     | The scalafmt formatting tasks, then `fix`: prepares the sources for a pull request                    |
| `publish-all` | `project /` then `+publishSigned`: signs and publishes all artifacts                                  |
| `quiet`       | `quiet on` mutes the welcome banner and `quiet off` shows it again                                    |

`addCommand(commands, name, description)` adds a command of your own that the welcome banner lists:

```scala
addCommand(List("scalafmtAll", "Test / compile"), "check-all", "Formats and compiles everything")
```

### Tasks

The plugin defines three tasks in `zio.sbt.Tasks`.

| Task                   | Description                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableStrictCompile`  | Sets the system property `enable.strict.compilation` to `true`                                                                    |
| `disableStrictCompile` | Sets the system property `enable.strict.compilation` to `false`                                                                   |
| `build`                | Runs `clean`, `enableStrictCompile`, `Compile / compile`, `Test / compile` and `Test / test`, then `disableStrictCompile`         |

The plugin's own settings do not read the `enable.strict.compilation` property. `stdSettings` adds `-Xfatal-warnings` on Scala 2 when the `CI` environment variable is set, whatever the property says. A build that wants warnings as errors only under `lint` can read the property in its own `scalacOptions`.

### Standard Settings

`stdSettings` is the entry point for configuring a project. Its parameters are:

| Parameter                       | Type             | Default | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                          | `Option[String]` | `None`  | Sets the sbt `name` when present                                                             |
| `packageName`                   | `Option[String]` | `None`  | Enables `buildInfoSettings` with this package for sbt-buildinfo when present                 |
| `javaPlatform`                  | `String`         | `"17"`  | Sets the `javaPlatform` setting and the `-source` and `-target` javac options                |
| `enableKindProjector`           | `Boolean`        | `true`  | Adds the kind-projector compiler plugin on Scala 2                                           |
| `enableCrossProject`            | `Boolean`        | `false` | Adds `crossProjectSettings`                        |
| `enableScalafix`                | `Boolean`        | `true`  | Adds `scalafixSettings`                                                                      |
| `turnCompilerWarningIntoErrors` | `Boolean`        | `true`  | Adds `-Xfatal-warnings` on Scala 2 when the `CI` environment variable is set                  |

Besides these, `stdSettings` adds the standard `scalacOptions` for the Scala version, runs `Test / parallelExecution` on Scala 2 only, enables `autoAPIMappings` and adds the better-monadic-for compiler plugin.

`stdSettings` takes the project name and, optionally, the package name for build info:

```scala
lazy val core = project
  .settings(stdSettings(name = Some("my-library"), packageName = Some("com.example.mylibrary")))
```

### Dependency and Platform Settings

These methods return sbt settings that a project adds with `.settings(...)`.

| Method                                                | Description                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableZIO(enableStreaming = false, enableTesting = true)` | Adds `zio` with `zioVersion`, plus `zio-streams` and the ZIO Test framework as requested            |
| `jsSettings`                                          | Settings for Scala.js projects: forks `Test` only on the JVM platform                               |
| `nativeSettings`                                      | Settings for Scala Native projects: skips `doc` and replaces `Test / test` with a compile of the tests, and forks `Test` only on the JVM platform      |
| `scalajs`                                             | Adds the `-scalajs` option on Scala 3                                                                |
| `scalafixSettings`                                    | Enables semanticdb (except on Scala 3) and adds the scaluzzi scalafix rules                                                                    |
| `scalaReflectTestSettings`                            | Adds `scala-reflect` in the `Test` configuration, from the Scala 2.13 version on Scala 3                                                            |
| `crossProjectSettings`                                | Adds the platform- and Scala-version-specific source directories (for example `scala-2.13+`, `scala-3.x`) to `Compile` and `Test`                           |
| `buildInfoSettings(packageName)`                      | Exposes `name`, `version`, `scalaVersion`, `sbtVersion` and `isSnapshot` in sbt-buildinfo            |
| `macroExpansionSettings`                              | Enables macro annotations on Scala 2.13 and the macro paradise plugin on 2.12                        |
| `macroDefinitionSettings`                             | Adds `-language:experimental.macros` and the provided `scala-reflect` and `scala-compiler` on Scala 2 |

`enableZIO` adds ZIO using `zioVersion`:

```scala
lazy val core = project
  .settings(enableZIO(enableStreaming = true))
```

### Version-Specific Helpers

Each helper takes the Scala binary versions it applies to, such as `"2.13"` or `"3"`, then the options or dependencies. The `optionsOn*` and `dependenciesOn*` methods return initializations and the `add*` methods return settings.

| Method                                     | Description                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `optionsOn(versions*)(options*)`           | The options when the Scala binary version is one of `versions`, an empty `Seq` otherwise           |
| `optionsOnExcept(versions*)(options*)`     | The options when the Scala binary version is none of `versions`                                    |
| `optionsOnOrElse(versions*)(options*)(other*)` | The options on the listed versions and the other options everywhere else                       |
| `addOptionsOn`, `addOptionsOnExcept`, `addOptionsOnOrElse` | The same three, as a setting that appends to `scalacOptions`                        |
| `dependenciesOn(versions*)(modules*)`      | The modules when the Scala binary version is one of `versions`                                     |
| `dependenciesOnExcept(versions*)(modules*)` | The modules when the Scala binary version is none of `versions`                                   |
| `dependenciesOnOrElse(versions*)(modules*)(other*)` | The modules on the listed versions and the other modules everywhere else                  |
| `addDependenciesOn`, `addDependenciesOnExcept`, `addDependenciesOnOrElse` | The same three, as a setting that appends to `libraryDependencies`           |

`addOptionsOn` adds compiler options for the listed Scala binary versions only:

```scala
addOptionsOn("2.13")("-Ymacro-annotations")
```

## ZIO SBT GitHub Actions

`zio-sbt-githubactions` is a Scala model of GitHub Actions workflows and of the config files of dependency bots. [ZIO SBT CI](./ci.md) uses it to render the generated YAML, and a build uses it to describe jobs, steps and triggers in `build.sbt`. The module is published as a dependency of `zio-sbt-ci`, so it needs no installation of its own. Its types live in the `zio.sbt.githubactions` package and are not exported through `autoImport`, so import them explicitly.

### Workflow Model

A `Workflow` holds a name, environment variables, triggers, jobs and an optional `Concurrency`. A `Job` holds steps and the settings of one GitHub Actions job. The following types make up the model.

| Type                  | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Workflow`            | Name, `env`, `triggers`, `jobs`, `concurrency` and `permissions`. `withoutPermissions` omits the `permissions` block, which is not the same as an empty map |
| `Job`                 | `id`, `name`, `runsOn`, `continueOnError`, `strategy`, `steps`, `need`, `services`, `condition`, `jobTimeout`, `concurrency` and `permissions`    |
| `Strategy`            | `Strategy(matrix, maxParallel = None, failFast = true)`, the matrix of a job                                                                      |
| `Step`                | `Step.SingleStep` has `name`, `id`, `uses`, `condition`, `parameters`, `run` and `env`. `Step.StepSequence` groups several steps                  |
| `ActionRef`           | The `uses` reference of a step, such as `actions/checkout@v7.0.1`                                                                                     |
| `Trigger`             | `WorkflowDispatch`, `Schedule`, `Release`, `PullRequest`, `PullRequestTarget`, `Push`, `Create`, `WorkflowRun` and `IssueComment`                 |
| `Branch`              | `Branch.All` or `Branch.Named(name)`, used by push and pull request triggers                                                                      |
| `Condition`           | `Condition.Expression(expression)` renders as `${{ expression }}`. `Condition.Function(expression)` renders as written. Both combine with `&&` and `\|\|`, but a `Function` cannot be combined |
| `Service`             | A service container: `name`, `image`, `env`, `ports` and `options`                                                                                |
| `ImageRef`            | The image of a service, such as `ImageRef("postgres:16")`                                                                                         |
| `ServicePort`         | `ServicePort(inner, outer)` renders as `inner:outer`                                                                                              |
| `Concurrency`         | `Concurrency(group, cancelInProgress = CancelInProgress.Always)`                                                                                  |
| `CancelInProgress`    | `Always`, `Never` or `When(condition)`                                                                                                            |
| `OS`                  | The runner operating system. `OS.UbuntuLatest` renders as `ubuntu-latest`                                                                         |

To change a job that a setting produced, copy it with the `Job` methods `withStrategy`, `withRunsOn`, `withSteps`, `withServices`, `withTimeout` and `withPermissions`. A job's `timeoutMinutes` field is deprecated in favor of `jobTimeout`.

The `zio.sbt.V` object resolves the pinned version of an action, so `V("actions/checkout")` returns the `actions/checkout@<version>` reference that the generated workflows use.

### CI Setting Types

These types are the values of the `ci*` settings of [ZIO SBT CI](./ci.md).

| Type                           | Used by                                          | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DependencyBot`                | `ciDependencyUpdateBots`                         | `Dependabot` (`dependabot[bot]`), `Renovate` (`renovate[bot]`), `ScalaSteward(githubAppName)` (`<githubAppName>[bot]`) and `Custom(login)` |
| `DeployPreviewMode`            | `ciDeployPreviewMode`                            | `Automatic` or `OnDemand`                                                                             |
| `DependabotConfig`             | `ciDependabotConfig`                             | `DependabotConfig(updates)`, by default one weekly `github-actions` update                            |
| `DependabotUpdate`             | `DependabotConfig`                               | `ecosystem`, `directory = "/"`, `interval = "weekly"`, `openPullRequestsLimit` and `groups`           |
| `DependabotGroup`              | `DependabotUpdate`                               | `name`, `patterns` and `updateTypes`                                                                  |
| `ScalaStewardConfig`           | `ciScalaStewardConfig`                           | The `.scala-steward.conf` content: `pins`, `allow`, `ignore`, `updatesLimit`, `updatePullRequests`, `commitMessage`, `pullRequestsFrequency`, `grouping`, `assignees` and `reviewers` |
| `ScalaStewardDependency`       | `ScalaStewardConfig`                             | `groupId`, `artifactId` and `version`                                                                 |
| `ScalaStewardGroupingRule`     | `ScalaStewardConfig`                             | `name` and a `filter` of `ScalaStewardGroupFilter(group, version)`                                    |
| `ReleaseDrafterCategory`       | `ciReleaseDrafterCategories`                     | `title` and the `labels` that put a pull request in the category                                      |
| `ReleaseDrafterVersionResolver`| `ciReleaseDrafterVersionResolver`                | The labels for `major`, `minor` and `patch`, and the `default` bump                                   |
| `ReleaseDrafterAutolabelerRule`| `ciReleaseDrafterAutolabeler`                    | A `label` and the `files`, `branch`, `title` and `body` patterns that apply it                        |

The how-to guides show these types at work. See [Auto-Approve and Auto-Merge Dependency Update PRs](../how-to-guides/auto-approve-and-auto-merge-dependency-update-prs.md), [Configure Dependabot Updates](../how-to-guides/configure-dependabot-updates.md) and [Customize the Generated CI Jobs](../how-to-guides/customize-the-generated-ci-jobs.md).

## ZIO SBT Source

ZIO SBT Source is a Scala 2.13 and Scala 3 cross-compiled library, not an sbt plugin, that provides utilities for self-documenting example code. It contains the `ExprEval` macro, which captures the source text of expressions at compile time and prints it alongside the evaluated result at runtime, `SourceFile` and `SourceReader`, which read source files, and `EmbedSourceModifier`, an mdoc modifier that embeds a source file into a documentation page.

### Installation

Add the following line to your `libraryDependencies` in the `build.sbt` of the docs project:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-sbt-source" % "0.8.12"
```

### ExprEval

`ExprEval.show` prints each expression followed by its value:

```scala
import zio.sbt.ExprEval.show

show(
  42 + 8,
  "Hello, " + "World!"
)
```

It prints:

```
42 + 8
// 50
"Hello, " + "World!"
// Hello, World!
```

#### Comment Labels

Consecutive `//` comment lines immediately above the `show` call are printed as a label above the output:

```scala
// Calculate the answer to life, the universe, and everything
show(6 * 7)
```

It prints:

```
// Calculate the answer to life, the universe, and everything
6 * 7
// 42
```

#### Block Form

`show` also accepts a block, with one expression per line:

```scala
show {
  1 + 2
  3 * 4
  "hello"
}
```

#### Implementation

The Scala 3 version is an `inline def` that uses `scala.quoted` to capture the source. The Scala 2.13 version is a whitebox macro that achieves the same. At runtime, `SourceReader` reads the comment lines above the call from the source file, and returns nothing when the file does not exist.

### SourceFile

`SourceFile` reads a source file and prints it as a fenced code block:

| Method                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SourceFile.readSource(path)`                            | Returns the file content. When `path` does not exist relative to the working directory, it is tried again relative to the parent directory   |
| `SourceFile.fileExtension(path)`                         | Returns the extension of the file name, used as the language of the fence                                                                    |
| `SourceFile.printSource(path, comment = true, showLineNumbers = false)` | Prints a code fence whose language is the file extension. With `comment` the fence has `title="<path>"`, and with `showLineNumbers` it has the `showLineNumbers` flag |

`SourceFile.printSource` prints a source file from an mdoc block:

```scala
import zio.sbt.SourceFile

SourceFile.printSource("path/to/Example.scala")
```

### EmbedSourceModifier

`EmbedSourceModifier` extends mdoc with the `embed` modifier. A code fence whose info string is `mdoc:embed:<path>` is replaced by the file at `<path>`, rendered with `SourceFile.printSource`. Leave the body of the fence empty:

```
\`\`\`scala mdoc:embed:path/to/Example.scala
\`\`\`
```

An empty path, or a file that cannot be read, is reported as an mdoc error.

#### Line Numbers

The `:showLineNumbers` flag, or its kebab-case alias `:show-line-numbers`, enables line numbers in [Docusaurus](https://docusaurus.io) code blocks:

```
\`\`\`scala mdoc:embed:path/to/Example.scala:showLineNumbers
\`\`\`
```

Both forms emit `showLineNumbers` in the code fence header.
