## How to Compress and Decompress a Stream

Every codec in this library is a `Compressor` or a `Decompressor`, so a stream can be compressed or decompressed by changing one value. This guide shows how to compress a file with any codec, decompress it again, and keep the codec choice in one place.

### Compress a File

A compressor is a pipeline. Read the file with `ZStream.fromFileName`, pipe it through the compressor, and write the result with `ZSink.fromFileName`. The function below takes any `Compressor`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

def compressFile(input: String, output: String, compressor: Compressor): ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName(input)
    .via(compressor.compress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName(output))
```

`run` returns the number of bytes written to `output`. The function works the same for Gzip, Zstd, LZ4, and any other codec.

### Decompress a File

Decompression is the same pipeline with a `Decompressor`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

def decompressFile(input: String, output: String, decompressor: Decompressor): ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName(input)
    .via(decompressor.decompress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName(output))
```

Use the decompressor that matches the compressor. Gzip data needs a Gzip decompressor, and Zstd data needs a Zstd decompressor.

### Choose a Codec in One Place

Keep the codec choice in a single value, so the rest of the program does not change when the choice does:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val compressorChoice: Compressor = GzipCompressor(deflateLevel = DeflateCompressionLevel(9))

val decompressorChoice: Decompressor = GzipDecompressor()
```

To switch to Zstd, replace the two values with `ZstdCompressor` and `ZstdDecompressor`. The functions above stay unchanged.

:::tip[Pick a codec by its trade-off]
Gzip is the most widely supported format. Zstd gives good compression at high speed. Brotli4J compresses text well at a high quality setting. LZ4 and Snappy favor speed over ratio. Bzip2 compresses well but uses a lot of memory. See the reference page of each codec for its options.
:::

### Round Trip a File

To check that a codec works for your data, compress a file, decompress the result, and compare the two:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

def gzipFile(input: String, output: String): ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName(input)
    .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName(output))

val roundTrip: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Boolean] =
  for {
    _ <- gzipFile("notes.txt", "notes.txt.gz")
    original <- ZStream.fromFileName("notes.txt").runCollect
    restored <- ZStream.fromFileName("notes.txt.gz").via(GzipDecompressor.decompress).runCollect
  } yield original == restored
```

Both sides are `Chunk[Byte]`, so `==` compares the bytes.

### Notes

- Compression is lazy. Nothing is read from the file until the pipeline runs.
- A codec may fail on invalid input. The error appears in the `Throwable` of the pipeline.
- To compress several files into one archive, see [Create and Read Archives](./how-to-create-and-read-archives.md).

## How to Create and Read Archives

An archive bundles several files into one stream of bytes. This guide shows how to build a ZIP or Tar archive from several entries, write it to a file, and read the entries back.

### Choose a Format

Pick the format that your consumers can open:

- Use ZIP with `ZipArchiver` when the archive is for Windows users or for tools that expect a ZIP file. ZIP entries can have unknown sizes when written, so `ZipArchiver` accepts any entry.
- Use Tar with `TarArchiver` when the archive is for Unix tooling. Tar entries must have a known size, and a tarball is usually compressed with Gzip afterwards.

### Build the Entries

Each entry is a pair of an `ArchiveEntry` and the stream of its content. Keep the entries in a stream, so that each file's content is read lazily:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val notes = "Meeting at 10:00".getBytes("UTF-8")
val todo = "Buy milk".getBytes("UTF-8")

val entries: ZStream[Any, Nothing, (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any], ZStream[Any, Nothing, Byte])] =
  ZStream.fromIterable(
    Seq(
      ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs", isDirectory = true) -> ZStream.empty,
      ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs/notes.txt") -> ZStream.fromIterable(notes),
      ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs/todo.txt") -> ZStream.fromIterable(todo),
    )
  )
```

The first entry is a directory, which is set with `isDirectory = true`. The writer adds the trailing `/` to the name. A name that ends in `/` without that flag is written as a file, so use the flag for directories.

### Write a ZIP Archive

Pipe the entries through `ZipArchiver` and write the result to a file:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val notes = "Meeting at 10:00".getBytes("UTF-8")

val writeZip: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream(
    ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs/notes.txt") -> ZStream.fromIterable(notes)
  ).via(ZipArchiver().archive)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName("docs.zip"))
```

`ZipArchiver().archive` writes deflated entries. To set the compression level, pass one to the constructor, for example `ZipArchiver(level = DeflateCompressionLevel(9))`, and call `archive` on that instance.

### Write a Tar Archive

`TarArchiver` requires every entry to declare its size, so each entry uses `withKnownUncompressedSize`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val notes = "Meeting at 10:00".getBytes("UTF-8")
val todo = "Buy milk".getBytes("UTF-8")

val writeTarGz: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream(
    ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs/notes.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(notes.length.toLong) -> ZStream.fromIterable(notes),
    ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("docs/todo.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(todo.length.toLong) -> ZStream.fromIterable(todo),
  ).via(TarArchiver().archive)
    .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName("docs.tar.gz"))
```

The `withKnownUncompressedSize` call is required here, because the tar writer only accepts `ArchiveEntry[Some, _]`. If the size does not match the bytes written, the stream dies with an `IllegalStateException`.

### Read a ZIP Archive

To read the entry names and sizes of a ZIP file, use `list`:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val listZip: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Chunk[String]] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("docs.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().list)
    .map(entry => s"${entry.name} (${entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L)} bytes)")
    .runCollect
```

To read the content as well, use `unarchive`, and read each entry before the next one is emitted. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) for the rules and for a size limit.

### Read a Tar Archive

Decompress the Gzip layer first, and then read the tar entries:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val listTarGz: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Chunk[String]] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("docs.tar.gz")
    .via(GzipDecompressor.decompress)
    .via(TarUnarchiver().list)
    .map(_.name)
    .runCollect
```

### Notes

- `ZipArchiver` accepts entries with or without a size. `TarArchiver` and `Zip4JArchiver` require the size.
- For password-protected ZIP archives, use the Zip4J module. See [Zip4J](./reference-zip4j.md).

---

## How to Read Archives Safely

Reading an archive means reading entries that someone else may have written. This guide shows how to read entry contents without losing data, and how to stop an entry that is too large before it fills the memory.

### Read Each Entry Before the Next One

Every unarchiver in this library emits entries in a streaming fashion. The content of an entry is a stream that reads from the archive directly. When you move on to the next entry without reading the current content, the pipeline waits for that content to be read. Nothing reads it, so the pipeline never continues. The program locks up and halts without an error.

For that reason, read each entry's content completely before the next entry is emitted. The simplest way is to run the content stream inside the `mapZIO` that handles the entry:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val printSizes =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("archive.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().unarchive)
    .mapZIO { case (archiveEntry, contentStream) =>
      contentStream.runCount.flatMap { count =>
        Console.printLine(s"${archiveEntry.name} has $count bytes")
      }
    }
    .runDrain
```

`ZStream#runCount` reads the whole entry and counts its bytes. The next entry waits until this one is finished.

If you only need the metadata of each entry, use `list` instead. `list` reads the content for you, and it fills in the uncompressed size. The same rule applies to all unarchivers.

The rule replaces the behavior of zio-streams-compress 1.x. In 1.x, consuming the next entry, even by accident, corrupted the content of every entry. For example, buffering or rechunking the entries before reading them did that. Since 2.0 the unarchiver reads each entry on demand, so it can keep streaming without corrupting content. The price is that each entry must be read before the next one starts.

### Rechunk, Buffer and Parallel Processing

Some operators need the next entry before they emit anything. Examples are `rechunk` with a size above one, `grouped`, and `zip`. If such an operator runs directly after `unarchive`, it asks for the second entry while the first one is still unread, so the pipeline locks up:

```scala
// Locks up: rechunk asks for the second entry before the first entry's content is read
ZStream.fromFileName("archive.zip").via(ZipUnarchiver().unarchive).rechunk(10)
```

Put these operators after the step that reads each entry's content. `buffer` and `mapZIOPar` follow the same rule: each step reads its entry's content before it returns. Once that holds, the entries can be processed in parallel and in batches:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val countBytes =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("archive.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().unarchive)
    .mapZIOPar(4) { case (archiveEntry, contentStream) =>
      contentStream.runCount.map(count => (archiveEntry.name, count))
    }
    .rechunk(10) // safe: each entry's content was read before its result is emitted
    .runDrain
```

Reading only part of an entry counts as not reading it. If you stop an entry's content early, for example with `take`, the next entry waits forever. The size-limit example below avoids this, because it fails the stream when an entry is too large instead of stopping early.

### Stop Entries That Are Too Large

An archive entry can claim any uncompressed size, and the claim can be wrong. Read at most a fixed number of bytes from each entry to protect the memory of your program. The size reported in the entry header is a hint, so check it and also count the bytes you actually read:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val maxEntrySize: Long = 10L * 1024 * 1024

val loadSmallEntries =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("archive.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().unarchive)
    .mapZIO { case (archiveEntry, contentStream) =>
      if (archiveEntry.uncompressedSize.exists(_ > maxEntrySize))
        ZIO.fail(new IllegalStateException(s"archive entry ${archiveEntry.name} is too large"))
      else
        contentStream.take(maxEntrySize + 1).runCollect.flatMap { content =>
          if (content.size > maxEntrySize)
            ZIO.fail(new IllegalStateException(s"archive entry ${archiveEntry.name} is too large"))
          else
            ZIO.succeed((archiveEntry.name, content))
        }
    }
    .rechunk(10)
```

The first check rejects entries that declare a large size. The second check handles entries that declare nothing, or declare a smaller size than their content. `take(maxEntrySize + 1)` reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to detect an overflow without reading the whole entry.

The `rechunk` after the check groups the entries into batches of ten, so later stages can process several at once. Rechunking is safe here because each entry's content has already been read in full.

### Choose Between List and Unarchive

Use `list` when you need the name and the size of each entry, and nothing else. Use `unarchive` when you need the content. The table shows the difference:

| Method      | Emits                                   | Reads content | Uncompressed size       |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------|
| `list`      | `ArchiveEntry`                          | Yes, to count | Always known            |
| `unarchive` | `ArchiveEntry` and its content stream   | No            | Only when the archive says so |

### Notes

- The uncompressed size from the archive header may be missing, wrong, or malicious. Count the bytes you read.
- A failure in one entry's content stream fails the whole archive stream. Handle the error in `mapZIO` if you want to skip the entry instead.
- For writing archives, see [Create and Read Archives](./how-to-create-and-read-archives.md).

## How to Read a Password-Protected ZIP

Some ZIP archives are protected by a password. The Zip4J module reads these archives, and the standard `zip` module does not. This guide shows how to list and read the entries of such an archive.

### Read the Entries

Pass the password to `Zip4JUnarchiver`. The reader uses the password to decrypt each entry as it reads it:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val listProtected: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Chunk[String]] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("secret.zip")
    .via(Zip4JUnarchiver(password = Some("it is a secret")).list)
    .map(entry => s"${entry.name} (${entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L)} bytes)")
    .runCollect
```

To read the content of each entry, use `unarchive` and read each entry's content before the next entry is emitted. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) for the rules. The example below prints the size of each entry's content:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val readProtected: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Unit] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("secret.zip")
    .via(Zip4JUnarchiver(password = Some("it is a secret")).unarchive)
    .mapZIO { case (entry, content) =>
      content.runCollect.flatMap { bytes =>
        Console.printLine(s"${entry.name}: ${bytes.size} bytes")
      }
    }
    .runDrain
```

### Use the Right Password

The password is a `String`, and Zip4J converts it to characters when it opens the archive. Keep the password out of the source code. Read it from an environment variable or a secret store, for example:

```scala
import zio._

val password: UIO[Option[String]] = ZIO.succeed(sys.env.get("ARCHIVE_PASSWORD"))
```

### Notes

- The module can read archives that use the traditional ZIP encryption, which the `zip -e` command produces.
- An archive without a password can be read with `Zip4JUnarchiver()`, or with `ZipUnarchiver` from the `zip` module.
- Writing a password-protected archive does not encrypt the entries yet. See the warning on the [Zip4J](./reference-zip4j.md) reference page.

## Compression and archives with zio-streams

[ZIO Streams Compress](https://github.com/zio/zio-streams-compress) integrates several compression algorithms and archive formats with [ZIO Streams](https://zio.dev). Every codec and archive format is a pipeline, so it fits into a stream with `via` like any other operator.

### Installation

To use the library, add one or more of the following lines to your `build.sbt` file:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-brotli" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-brotli4j" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-bzip2" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-gzip" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-lz4" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-snappy" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-tar" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zip" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zip4j" % "3.0.1"
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zstd" % "3.0.1"
```

Each module depends on `core`, which is pulled in automatically. Add only the modules you use.

_As of 2.1.3, zio-streams-compress requires zio 2.1.25 or later._

The library is published for Scala 3, 2.13, and 2.12, and runs on the JVM. Scala.js and Scala Native are not supported. PRs for them are welcome.

### Choosing a Codec

The table lists each codec with its module. Compression and decompression are both available unless the table says otherwise.

| Format      | Module       | Compress | Decompress | Notes                                             |
|-------------|--------------|----------|------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Gzip        | `gzip`       | Yes      | Yes        | Widely supported. Built on the JDK.               |
| Zstd        | `zstd`       | Yes      | Yes        | Good ratio at high speed. Dictionary on write only. |
| Brotli      | `brotli`     | No       | Yes        | Decompression only, pure Java.                    |
| Brotli      | `brotli4j`   | Yes      | Yes        | Compresses text well. Loads a native library.     |
| Bzip2       | `bzip2`      | Yes      | Yes        | Good ratio. Uses a lot of memory.                 |
| LZ4         | `lz4`        | Yes      | Yes        | Very fast. Favors speed over ratio.               |
| Snappy      | `snappy`     | Yes      | Yes        | Fast. Three write formats.                        |
| ZIP         | `zip`        | Yes      | Yes        | Archive format. Entries may have unknown size.    |
| ZIP         | `zip4j`      | Yes      | Yes        | Archive format. Reads password-protected archives. |
| Tar         | `tar`        | Yes      | Yes        | Archive format. No compression of its own.        |

For a bundle of files, pick an archive format (ZIP or Tar). For a single stream of bytes, pick a codec. A `.tar.gz` file is a Tar archive wrapped in Gzip.

### Core Concepts

The library has two families of pipeline. A compressor turns bytes into compressed bytes, and a decompressor does the reverse. An archiver turns a stream of named entries into the bytes of an archive, and an unarchiver does the reverse. Every codec in the table is a compressor, a decompressor, or both. Every archive format is an archiver, an unarchiver, or both.

The [Core Interfaces](./reference-core.md) reference describes these types in full. The [Tutorial](./tutorial-compress-and-archive.md) builds a small program that uses them.

### Example

The example below compresses a file with Gzip, lists the entries of a Tar archive compressed with Gzip, and creates a ZIP archive:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

object ExampleApp extends ZIOAppDefault {
  override def run: ZIO[Any, Any, Any] =
    for {
      // Compress a file with Gzip
      _ <- ZStream
             .fromFileName("file")
             .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
             .run(ZSink.fromFileName("file.gz"))

      // List all items in a gzipped tar archive
      _ <- ZStream
             .fromFileName("file.tgz")
             .via(GzipDecompressor.decompress)
             .via(TarUnarchiver().list)
             .mapZIO { entry =>
               Console.printLine(s"${entry.name} ${entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L)}")
             }
             .runDrain

      // Create a ZIP archive with one entry
      _ <- ZStream(entry("file1.txt", "Hello world!".getBytes("UTF-8")))
             .via(ZipArchiver().archive)
             .run(ZSink.fromFileName("file.zip"))
    } yield ()

  private def entry(
    name: String,
    content: Array[Byte],
  ): (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any], ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte]) =
    (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any](name), ZStream.fromIterable(content))
}
```

The Zip4J module also supports encryption and decryption of zip files. See the [Zip4J](./reference-zip4j.md) reference.

### Unarchiving

As of zio-streams-compress 2.0, all unarchivers require the consumer to fully read the entry's contents before the next archive entry is emitted.

⚠️ Not reading the entry's content causes the unarchive pipeline to lock up and halt your program.

In zio-streams-compress 1.x, consuming the next archive entry, even by accident for example by using buffering or rechunking, corrupts the content stream of all archive entries. With the new requirement the unarchiver can continue to operate in a streaming fashion without corrupting content.

Most of the time the new requirement should not be an issue. For example, you can concatenate `unarchive` and `archive` pipelines without problems.

Two cases need care:

- You only need the metadata of the entries. Use the unarchiver's `list` method, which reads each entry's content behind the scenes.
- You need buffering, aggregation, rechunking or parallel processing to improve throughput. Read each entry's content in the step that handles the entry, then do the buffering, aggregation or parallel work. The [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) guide shows how, and how to limit the size of each entry.

- [How to Compress and Decompress a Stream](./how-to-compress-and-decompress.md) shows how to switch codecs.
- [How to Create and Read Archives](./how-to-create-and-read-archives.md) covers ZIP and Tar.
- [How to Read a Password-Protected ZIP](./how-to-read-password-protected-zip.md) reads Zip4J archives.

## Brotli

The `brotli` module decompresses the Brotli format. It is built on the official Brotli Java decoder, which is pure Java. This module does not compress. To compress Brotli, use the [Brotli4J](./reference-brotli4j.md) module, which compresses and decompresses.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-brotli" % "3.0.1"
```

### BrotliDecompressor

`BrotliDecompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the Brotli format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.br").via(BrotliDecompressor.decompress)
```

To read data that was compressed with a custom dictionary, pass the same dictionary to `BrotliDecompressor.apply`:

```scala
import zio.compress._

def dictionaryDecompressor(dictionary: Array[Byte]): BrotliDecompressor =
  BrotliDecompressor(customDictionary = Some(dictionary))
```

### Options

| Option             | Type                       | Default                             |
|--------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `customDictionary` | `Option[Array[Byte]]`      | `None` (no dictionary)              |
| `chunkSize`        | `Int`                      | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)  |

The `chunkSize` is the largest chunk emitted by the output stream.

### Notes

- The decompressor's error type is `Throwable`. Input that is not valid Brotli fails the stream.
- This module cannot produce Brotli data. Use `Brotli4JCompressor` for that.

---

## Brotli4J

The `brotli4j` module compresses and decompresses the Brotli format. It is built on the [Brotli4J](https://github.com/hyperxpro/Brotli4j) library, which loads a native Brotli library at runtime. The module loads that library the first time a pipeline runs.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-brotli4j" % "3.0.1"
```

### Brotli4JCompressor

`Brotli4JCompressor` is a `Compressor` that writes the Brotli format. Use `Brotli4JCompressor.apply` to set its options, or `Brotli4JCompressor.compress` for the library defaults:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(Brotli4JCompressor.compress)
```

To choose a quality, a window size, and a mode:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val tuned = Brotli4JCompressor(
  quality = BrotliQuality(11),
  lgwin = BrotliLogWindow(22),
  mode = Some(BrotliMode.Text),
)
```

`BrotliQuality(11)` and `BrotliLogWindow(22)` return an `Option`, which matches the parameter types directly.

### Brotli4JDecompressor

`Brotli4JDecompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the Brotli format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.br").via(Brotli4JDecompressor.decompress)
```

### Options

| Option    | Type                              | Default                             |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `quality` | `Option[BrotliQuality]`           | `None` (the library default)        |
| `lgwin`   | `Option[BrotliLogWindow]`         | `None` (the library default)        |
| `mode`    | `Option[BrotliMode]`              | `None` (the library default)        |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (decompressor only)       | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)  |

`BrotliQuality` ranges from 0 to 11. Higher values compress more and run slower. Named constants `Quality0` to `Quality11` exist for each value.

`BrotliLogWindow` is the base-2 logarithm of the LZ window size. It ranges from 10 to 24. Larger windows find more matches in large inputs.

`BrotliMode` gives the encoder a hint about the input:

- `BrotliMode.Generic` makes no assumption about the input. This is the default behaviour of the library.
- `BrotliMode.Text` is for UTF-8 text.
- `BrotliMode.Font` is for the WOFF 2.0 font format.

### Notes

- Both the compressor and the decompressor fail with a `Throwable` when the native library cannot be loaded, or when the input is not valid Brotli.
- Use this module instead of [Brotli](./reference-brotli.md) when you need to compress.

---

## Bzip2

The `bzip2` module compresses and decompresses the Bzip2 format. It is built on the Apache Commons Compress library.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-bzip2" % "3.0.1"
```

### Bzip2Compressor

`Bzip2Compressor` is a `Compressor` that writes the Bzip2 format. Use `Bzip2Compressor.apply` to set the block size, or `Bzip2Compressor.compress` for the default block size:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(Bzip2Compressor.compress)
```

To write blocks of 100 KB instead of the default 900 KB:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val smallBlocks = Bzip2Compressor(blockSize = Bzip2BlockSize(1))
```

`Bzip2BlockSize(1)` returns an `Option`, which matches the `blockSize` parameter type.

Bzip2 uses a lot of memory. The memory needed grows with the block size. See the [Apache Commons Compress documentation](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-compress/javadocs/api-1.28.0/org/apache/commons/compress/compressors/bzip2/BZip2CompressorOutputStream.html) for the heap needed for each block size.

### Bzip2Decompressor

`Bzip2Decompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the Bzip2 format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.bz2").via(Bzip2Decompressor.decompress)
```

### Options

| Option      | Type                          | Default                             |
|-------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `blockSize` | `Option[Bzip2BlockSize]`      | `None` (900 KB)                     |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (decompressor only)     | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)  |

`Bzip2BlockSize` ranges from 1 to 9, in units of 100 KB. Named constants `BlockSize100KB` to `BlockSize900KB` exist for each value. A larger block size gives a better compression ratio and needs more memory.

### Notes

- Both pipelines fail with a `Throwable` when the input is not valid Bzip2.
- Bzip2 compresses one stream at a time. It has no entry names or metadata. To compress several files, use a tar archive inside the Bzip2 stream.

## Core Interfaces

The `core` module defines the interfaces that every codec and archive format in ZIO Streams Compress implements. Each codec module depends on `core`, so these types are always available once you add any other module from the [installation instructions](./index.md#installation).

Most users never implement these interfaces. They are useful for understanding what the codecs have in common and for writing code that accepts any codec.

### Compressor and Decompressor

A `Compressor` turns a raw byte stream into a compressed byte stream. A `Decompressor` does the reverse. Both expose a single pipeline:

```scala
trait Compressor {
  def compress: ZPipeline[Any, Throwable, Byte, Byte]
}

trait Decompressor {
  def decompress: ZPipeline[Any, Throwable, Byte, Byte]
}
```

Because every codec exposes the same shape, a function can accept any compressor:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

def compressText(compressor: Compressor, text: String): ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable(text.getBytes("UTF-8")).via(compressor.compress)
```

`Compressor.empty` and `Decompressor.empty` pass bytes through unchanged. They are useful as a default when the caller does not want compression:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val compressorOrNone: Compressor = Compressor.empty
```

### Archiver and Unarchiver

An `Archiver` takes a stream of archive entries and produces the bytes of an archive. Each entry is a pair of an `ArchiveEntry` and the content stream for that entry:

```scala
trait Archiver[-Size[A] <: Option[A]] {
  def archive: ZPipeline[
    Any,
    Throwable,
    (ArchiveEntry[Size, Any], ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte]),
    Byte,
  ]
}
```

An `Unarchiver` does the reverse. It takes the bytes of an archive and produces the entries with their content:

```scala
trait Unarchiver[Size[A] <: Option[A], Underlying] {
  def unarchive: ZPipeline[
    Any,
    Throwable,
    Byte,
    (ArchiveEntry[Size, Underlying], ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte]),
  ]

  def list: ZPipeline[Any, Throwable, Byte, ArchiveEntry[Some, Underlying]]
}
```

`Unarchiver#list` returns the entries with their uncompressed size filled in. It reads each entry's content to count the bytes, so it is slower than `unarchive` on large archives. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) for the rules that apply to `unarchive`.

### ArchiveEntry

`ArchiveEntry` describes one entry in an archive:

```scala
final case class ArchiveEntry[+Size[A] <: Option[A], +Underlying](
  name: String,
  uncompressedSize: Size[Long] = Option.empty[Long],
  isDirectory: Boolean = false,
  lastModified: Option[Instant] = None,
  lastAccess: Option[Instant] = None,
  creation: Option[Instant] = None,
)
```

The type parameter `Size` says whether the uncompressed size is known:

| Size    | Meaning                                  | Used by                                      |
|---------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `Some`  | The uncompressed size is always present  | Writing with `Zip4JArchiver` and `TarArchiver` |
| `None`  | The uncompressed size is never present   | No built-in module writes it                |
| `Option`| The uncompressed size may or may not be present | Writing with `ZipArchiver`; reading with every unarchiver |

Create an entry with its name, and optionally its size. The `with*` methods copy an entry with one field changed:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import java.time.Instant

val withoutSize: ArchiveEntry[Option, Any] = ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt")

val withSize: ArchiveEntry[Some, Any] =
  ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(12L)

val dir: ArchiveEntry[Option, Any] =
  ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes").withIsDirectory(true)

val timestamped: ArchiveEntry[Option, Any] =
  withoutSize.withLastModified(Some(Instant.parse("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z")))
```

When the entry comes from a reader, `ArchiveEntry#underlying` gives the library object it was built from. The type depends on the archive format, for example `ZipEntry` for `ZipUnarchiver`.

### Size Requirements on Write

Some archive formats must know the size of each entry before its content is written. The `Size` type parameter enforces this at compile time:

- `Zip4JArchiver` and `TarArchiver` require `ArchiveEntry[Some, _]`. Use `withKnownUncompressedSize` or `ArchiveEntry[Some, Any](name, Some(size))`.
- `ZipArchiver` accepts `ArchiveEntry[Option, _]`, so the size may be omitted.

The writers that check sizes compare the number of bytes actually written with the declared size. A mismatch kills the stream with an `IllegalStateException`, which ZIO reports as a defect rather than a typed error. The check is a pipeline you can also apply yourself: `Archiver.checkUncompressedSize`.

### ArchiveSingleFileCompressor and ArchiveSingleFileDecompressor

These two helpers turn an archiver or unarchiver into a `Compressor` or `Decompressor` for a stream that holds exactly one file. They are useful for formats such as a zipped single file where the caller wants a plain byte pipeline.

`ArchiveSingleFileCompressor.forName` wraps a file name, with the size when the archiver requires it:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val zipOneFile = ArchiveSingleFileCompressor.forName(ZipArchiver(), "data.csv")

val tarOneFile = ArchiveSingleFileCompressor.forName(TarArchiver(), "data.csv", 1024L)
```

`ArchiveSingleFileDecompressor` takes an unarchiver and emits the content of the first non-directory entry. It drops the name, so use it only when the archive is known to hold one file. This example wraps a ZIP unarchiver:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val unzipOneFile = ArchiveSingleFileDecompressor(ZipUnarchiver())
```

### Chunk Sizes and Defaults

The `Defaults` object holds the shared values for the modules:

- `Defaults.DefaultChunkSize` is 64 KiB. It is the default buffer size for the gzip compressor and decompressor, and the chunk size for `ZipUnarchiver`, `TarUnarchiver`, and `Zip4JUnarchiver`.
- `Defaults.DefaultChunkedQueueSize` is 2. It is the size of the internal queue between a pipeline and the Java stream it wraps.

Some codecs use ZIO's own default of 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`) for their decompressors. Each reference page states the default for its module.

### Compression Levels

`DeflateCompressionLevel` is shared by the gzip and zip modules. Its `apply` method returns an `Option`, because only levels 0 to 9 are valid:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val level: Option[DeflateCompressionLevel] = DeflateCompressionLevel(9)

val invalid: Option[DeflateCompressionLevel] = DeflateCompressionLevel(10)

val best: DeflateCompressionLevel = DeflateCompressionLevel.BestCompressionLevel
```

Named constants exist for each level, plus `NoCompressionLevel`, `FastestCompressionLevel`, `DefaultCompressionLevel`, and `BestCompressionLevel`.

---

## Gzip

The `gzip` module compresses and decompresses the Gzip format. It is built on the ZIO Streams compression support, which uses the JVM standard library.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-gzip" % "3.0.1"
```

### GzipCompressor

`GzipCompressor` is a `Compressor` that writes the Gzip format. Create one with `GzipCompressor.apply` to set its options, or use `GzipCompressor.compress` for the defaults:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val gzipped: ZStream[Any, Nothing, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(GzipCompressor.compress)
```

To choose the compression level and strategy:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val fastest = GzipCompressor(
  deflateLevel = DeflateCompressionLevel(1),
  deflateStrategy = Some(DeflateStrategy.HuffmanOnly),
)
```

`DeflateCompressionLevel(1)` returns an `Option`, which matches the parameter type directly. When the value is invalid, pass `None` instead of a level.

### GzipDecompressor

`GzipDecompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the Gzip format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val unzipped: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.gz").via(GzipDecompressor.decompress)
```

The decompressor accepts several concatenated Gzip members in one input and emits their content in order. This is the form that results from appending the output of several compressions to one file.

### Options

| Option           | Type                                    | Default                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `deflateLevel`   | `Option[DeflateCompressionLevel]`       | `None` (ZIO's default, level 6) |
| `deflateStrategy`| `Option[DeflateStrategy]`               | `None` (default strategy)       |
| `bufferSize`     | `Int` (compressor and decompressor)     | 64 KiB                          |

`DeflateCompressionLevel` ranges from 0 (no compression) to 9 (best compression). See [Core Interfaces](./reference-core.md#compression-levels) for the named constants.

`DeflateStrategy` has two values:

- `DeflateStrategy.Filtered` suits data that a predictor filter has already transformed into many small values. It matches the zlib `Z_FILTERED` strategy.
- `DeflateStrategy.HuffmanOnly` skips string matching and only applies Huffman coding. It is fast, but compresses less.

The `bufferSize` is the largest chunk emitted by the output stream.

### Notes

- The compressor's error type is `Nothing`, so it cannot fail. Errors come from the upstream stream, not from compression.
- The decompressor fails with a `Throwable` when the input is not valid Gzip.
- The Gzip format is a single-file format. To compress several files into one archive, use a tar archive with Gzip around it. See [Tar](./reference-tar.md).

---

## LZ4

The `lz4` module compresses and decompresses the LZ4 frame format. It is built on the official LZ4 Java library.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-lz4" % "3.0.1"
```

### Lz4Compressor

`Lz4Compressor` is a `Compressor` that writes the LZ4 frame format. Use `Lz4Compressor.apply` to choose the block size, or `Lz4Compressor.compress` for the default block size:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(Lz4Compressor.compress)
```

To write blocks of 4 MiB:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val largeBlocks = Lz4Compressor(Lz4CompressorBlockSize.BlockSize4MiB)
```

### Lz4Decompressor

`Lz4Decompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the LZ4 frame format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.lz4").via(Lz4Decompressor.decompress)
```

### Options

| Option      | Type                          | Default                             |
|-------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `blockSize` | `Lz4CompressorBlockSize`      | 256 KiB                             |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (decompressor only)     | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)  |

`Lz4CompressorBlockSize` has four values: `BlockSize64KiB`, `BlockSize256KiB`, `BlockSize1MiB`, and `BlockSize4MiB`. A larger block size compresses better and uses more memory. To convert the numeric indicator of the LZ4 format (4 to 7), use `Lz4CompressorBlockSize.fromLz4BlockSizeIndicator`. It returns an `Option`, because other values are not valid.

### Notes

- Both pipelines fail with a `Throwable` when the input is not a valid LZ4 frame.
- The LZ4 frame format has no entry names or metadata. To compress several files, use a tar archive inside the LZ4 stream.

---

## Snappy

The `snappy` module compresses and decompresses the Snappy format. It is built on the [snappy-java](https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java) library.

Snappy has several incompatible variants. Before you choose a format, read the [snappy-java compatibility notes](https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java/blob/master/README.md#compatibility-notes).

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-snappy" % "3.0.1"
```

### SnappyCompressor

`SnappyCompressor` is a `Compressor` that writes Snappy. It takes a write format. The default is the framed format, and `SnappyCompressor.compress` uses that default:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(SnappyCompressor.compress)
```

To write the basic format with 64 KiB blocks:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val basic = SnappyCompressor(SnappyWriteFormat.Basic(blockSize = 64 * 1024))
```

### SnappyDecompressor

`SnappyDecompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads Snappy. It takes a read format. The default is the framed format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.sz").via(SnappyDecompressor.decompress)
```

### Write Formats

`SnappyWriteFormat` has three variants:

| Variant                         | Options and defaults                                                                  |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `SnappyWriteFormat.Framed`      | `blockSize` 64 KiB, must be 1 to 64 KiB. `minCompressionRatio` 0.85, must be in (0, 1].|
| `SnappyWriteFormat.Basic`       | `blockSize` 32 KiB, must be 1 KiB to 512 MiB.                                         |
| `SnappyWriteFormat.HadoopCompatible` | `blockSize` 32 KiB, must be 1 KiB to 512 MiB. Writes no file header.             |

`Framed` follows the [Snappy framing format](https://github.com/google/snappy/blob/master/framing_format.txt). The `minCompressionRatio` is the smallest ratio of compressed to raw size that must be reached before a block is written compressed. Blocks that do not reach it are stored uncompressed.

`Basic` writes the raw Snappy format, with no framing. `HadoopCompatible` writes the format of Hadoop and Spark, which puts the block size before each block.

An invalid option, such as a block size out of range, throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when you create the format.

### Read Formats

`SnappyReadFormat` has two variants:

| Variant                     | Options and defaults                                                                   |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `SnappyReadFormat.Framed`   | `verifyChecksums` `true`. When `true`, checksums in the input are verified.            |
| `SnappyReadFormat.Basic`    | `maxChunkSize` 512 MiB, must be 1 to 512 MiB. The largest number of bytes compressed together. |

Read the input with the format it was written with. The formats are not compatible with each other, so a mismatch produces errors or wrong output.

### Options

| Option      | Type                          | Default                             |
|-------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `format`    | `SnappyWriteFormat` (compressor) or `SnappyReadFormat` (decompressor) | `Framed()` |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (decompressor only)     | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)  |

---

## Tar

The `tar` module creates and reads Tar archives. It is built on the Apache Commons Compress library. A tar archive bundles files but does not compress them, so a compressed tarball is a tar archive wrapped in a codec such as Gzip.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-tar" % "3.0.1"
```

### TarArchiver

`TarArchiver` is an `Archiver` that writes Tar archives. Every entry must have a known uncompressed size, so the entry type is `ArchiveEntry[Some, _]`:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val content = "Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")

val entry = ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(content.length.toLong)

val tar = ZStream((entry, ZStream.fromIterable(content))).via(TarArchiver().archive)
```

If the number of bytes written does not match the declared size, the stream dies with an `IllegalStateException`.

To write a compressed tarball, pipe the archive through a compressor. The example uses Gzip:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val content = "Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")

val entry = ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(content.length.toLong)

val tarGz = ZStream((entry, ZStream.fromIterable(content)))
  .via(TarArchiver().archive)
  .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
```

### TarUnarchiver

`TarUnarchiver` is an `Unarchiver` that reads Tar archives. Each entry comes with its content as a stream. To read a compressed tarball, decompress first:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val names = ZStream
  .fromFileName("archive.tar.gz")
  .via(GzipDecompressor.decompress)
  .via(TarUnarchiver().list)
  .map(_.name)
```

`TarUnarchiver#list` reads each entry's content to fill in the uncompressed size. `TarUnarchiver#unarchive` gives the content as a stream, and it must be fully read before the next entry is emitted. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md).

### Options

| Option      | Type               | Default |
|-------------|--------------------|---------|
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (unarchiver) | 64 KiB  |

`TarArchiver` takes no options.

### Entry Metadata

Tar entries carry a name, a size, and optional timestamps. `TarArchiver` writes the `lastModified`, `lastAccess`, and `creation` fields of an `ArchiveEntry` when they are set. Set `isDirectory` to `true` to write a directory entry, and the name gets a trailing `/`.

When an entry's `underlying` value is a `TarArchiveEntry` with the same directory flag, the writer copies that entry's header and then applies the name and the fields set on the `ArchiveEntry`.

### Notes

- The archiver checks the size of each entry against the bytes it receives, and dies with an `IllegalStateException` on a mismatch.
- The unarchiver's error type is `IOException` for the entry content, and `Throwable` for the archive structure.
- Tar has no compression of its own. Use [Gzip](./reference-gzip.md) for `.tar.gz` files.

---

## Zip

The `zip` module creates and reads ZIP archives. It is built on the JVM standard library's ZIP support. For password-protected archives, use the [Zip4J](./reference-zip4j.md) module instead. Also use the Zip4J module when you need to use the 'Stored' zip-method and the archive entries are large, as this module needs to pull the full content of each entry in memory to calculate a checksum.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zip" % "3.0.1"
```

### ZipArchiver

`ZipArchiver` is an `Archiver` that writes ZIP archives. Its entries do not need a known size, so you can stream content of unknown length. Use `ZipArchiver.apply` to set the compression level and method, or `ZipArchiver.archive` for the defaults:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val files = ZStream.fromIterable(
  Seq(
    ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt") -> ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")),
    ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes", isDirectory = true) -> ZStream.empty,
  )
)

val archive: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] = files.via(ZipArchiver().archive)
```

Set `isDirectory` to `true` to write a directory entry; the writer adds the trailing `/` to the name. A name that ends in `/` without `isDirectory` is written as a file, with the slash removed.

### ZipUnarchiver

`ZipUnarchiver` is an `Unarchiver` that reads ZIP archives. Each entry comes with its content as a stream:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val entries: ZStream[Any, Throwable, (String, Long)] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("archive.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().list)
    .map(entry => entry.name -> entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L))
```

`ZipUnarchiver#list` reads each entry's content to fill in the uncompressed size. To process the content itself, use `ZipUnarchiver#unarchive` instead, and read each entry's content before the next entry is emitted. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) for the rules.

### Options

| Option      | Type                                         | Default                          |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `level`     | `Option[DeflateCompressionLevel]` (archiver) | `None` (zlib's default, level 6) |
| `zipMethod` | `ZipMethod` (archiver)                       | `Deflated`                       |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (unarchiver)                           | 64 KiB                           |

`level` applies only to deflated entries. `ZipMethod` has two values: `ZipMethod.Deflated` compresses each entry, and `ZipMethod.Stored` writes each entry without compression.

### Stored Entries

`ZipMethod.Stored` only works in v3.0.0 and later, earlier versions produced broken zip files.

Zip support from the JVM requires a CRC32 to be calculated up front. To do this, the full content of each entry is pulled into memory. The Zip4J module does not do this, and will have lower memory usage.

### Notes

- The archive format has no encryption in this module. Use [Zip4J](./reference-zip4j.md) to read password-protected archives.
- The archiver does not check the size of each entry, because the size is optional for this format.
- The unarchiver's error type is `IOException` for the entry content, and `Throwable` for the archive structure.

---

## Zip4J

The `zip4j` module creates and reads ZIP archives with the [Zip4J](https://github.com/srikanth-lingala/zip4j) library. Use it when you need to read password-protected archives. It requires every entry to declare its uncompressed size when you write one. Use the `Zip` module when you cannot provide the uncompressed size up front.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zip4j" % "3.0.1"
```

### Reading Archives

`Zip4JUnarchiver` is an `Unarchiver` that reads ZIP archives. Each entry comes with its content as a stream. Use `Zip4JUnarchiver.apply` with a password for a password-protected archive:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val contents: ZStream[Any, Throwable, (String, Long)] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("secret.zip")
    .via(Zip4JUnarchiver(password = Some("it is a secret")).list)
    .map(entry => entry.name -> entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L))
```

For an archive without a password, omit the `password` argument, or pass `None`:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val unprotected = ZStream.fromFileName("archive.zip").via(Zip4JUnarchiver().unarchive)
```

`Zip4JUnarchiver#list` reads each entry's content to fill in the uncompressed size. `Zip4JUnarchiver#unarchive` gives the content as a stream, and it must be fully read before the next entry is emitted. See [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md).

### Writing Archives

`Zip4JArchiver` is an `Archiver` that writes ZIP archives. Every entry must have a known uncompressed size, so the entry type is `ArchiveEntry[Some, _]`:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val content = "Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")

val entry = ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(content.length.toLong)

val archive = ZStream((entry, ZStream.fromIterable(content))).via(Zip4JArchiver().archive)
```

If the number of bytes written does not match the declared size, the stream dies with an `IllegalStateException`.

:::warning[Standard encryption is very weak]
`Zip4JArchiver(password = Some(...))` uses the standard Zip encryption which is very weak. Use `Zip4JArchiver.encrypted(...)` to set a better encryption method (see below).
:::

:::warning[Encrypting with 1.x or 2.x]
Prior to version 3.0.0, `Zip4JArchiver(password = Some(...))` does not encrypt the entries. The archive it writes is identical to the archive written without a password. Do not rely on this option to protect data. Reading password-protected archives works.
:::

### Options

| Option      | Type                   | Default              |
|-------------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `password`  | `Option[String]`       | `None` (no password) |
| `zipMethod` | `ZipMethod` (archiver) | `Deflated`           |
| `chunkSize` | `Int` (unarchiver)     | 64 KiB               |

`Zip4JUnarchiver` uses the password to decrypt encrypted entries.

### Entry Metadata

The entries that `Zip4JUnarchiver` returns include the name, the uncompressed size, and the `lastModified` timestamp, when the archive records them. An entry whose name ends in `/` is a directory.

### Writing Encrypted Archives

`Zip4JArchiver.encrypted(...)` makes a zip archiver that writes encrypted ZIP archives and also allows you to set the encryption method and zip method.

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.compress.zip4j._
import zio.stream._

val content = "Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")

val entry = ArchiveEntry[Option, Any]("notes/readme.txt").withKnownUncompressedSize(content.length.toLong)

val archive = ZStream((entry, ZStream.fromIterable(content)))
                .via(Zip4JArchiver.encrypted("password", EncryptionMethod.AES_256).archive)
```

### Notes

- The unarchiver's error type is `IOException` for the entry content, and `Throwable` for the archive structure.
- Use [Zip](./reference-zip.md) for archives without a password. It accepts entries whose size is not known in advance.

---

## Zstd

The `zstd` module compresses and decompresses the Zstandard format. It wraps the `com.github.luben:zstd-jni` library, which binds the native Zstandard library.

Add the module to your `build.sbt`:

```sbt
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zstd" % "3.0.1"
```

### ZstdCompressor

`ZstdCompressor` is a `Compressor` that writes the Zstandard format. Use `ZstdCompressor.apply` to set its options, or `ZstdCompressor.compress` for the library defaults:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromIterable("Hello, ZIO!".getBytes("UTF-8")).via(ZstdCompressor.compress)
```

To choose a level and use several worker threads:

```scala
import zio.compress._

val tuned = ZstdCompressor(
  level = ZstdCompressionLevel(19),
  workers = Some(4),
)
```

`ZstdCompressionLevel(19)` returns an `Option`, which matches the type of the `level` option. A level that is out of range gives `None`, and the library default applies.

### ZstdDecompressor

`ZstdDecompressor` is a `Decompressor` that reads the Zstandard format:

```scala
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressed: ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte] =
  ZStream.fromFileName("file.zst").via(ZstdDecompressor.decompress)
```

### Options

| Option             | Type                             | Default                                    |
|--------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `level`            | `Option[ZstdCompressionLevel]`   | `None` (the library default, level 3)      |
| `workers`          | `Option[Int]`                    | `None` (the library default)               |
| `customDictionary` | `Option[Array[Byte]]`            | `None` (no dictionary)                     |
| `chunkSize`        | `Int` (decompressor only)        | 4 KiB (`ZStream.DefaultChunkSize`)         |

`ZstdCompressionLevel` ranges from -131072 to 22. Negative levels trade compression ratio for speed. Named constants cover the common cases:

- `ZstdCompressionLevel.FastCompressionLevel` is -4.
- `ZstdCompressionLevel.DefaultCompressionLevel` is 3.
- `ZstdCompressionLevel.HighCompressionLevel` is 6.
- `ZstdCompressionLevel.VeryHighCompressionLevel` is 19.
- `ZstdCompressionLevel.UltraCompressionLevel` is 22. Levels 20 to 22 need a lot of memory.

`workers` is the number of threads for compression. Use `Some(0)` to detect the number of CPU cores. The library limits the number of workers it runs.

### Notes

- The decompressor accepts no dictionary. Data compressed with a `customDictionary` cannot be decompressed by this module.
- The compressor's error type is `Throwable`, because the native library can fail.
- Input that is not valid Zstandard fails the stream with a `Throwable`.

---

## Tutorial: Compress and Archive Files

Welcome! In this tutorial you will compress a text file with Gzip, then bundle several files into a ZIP archive and read the archive back. Each step builds on the one before. By the end, you will have a small program that does all of it.

You need Scala and sbt, and a project with ZIO Streams. The steps use the `gzip` and `zip` modules, which need only ZIO Streams and the JDK.

### Step 1: Add the Dependencies

Add the two modules to your `build.sbt` file:

```sbt
libraryDependencies ++= Seq(
  "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-gzip" % "3.0.1",
  "dev.zio" %% "zio-streams-compress-zip" % "3.0.1",
)
```

The `gzip` module provides `GzipCompressor` and `GzipDecompressor`. The `zip` module provides `ZipArchiver` and `ZipUnarchiver`. Both modules depend on `core`, which is pulled in automatically.

### Step 2: Compress a File with Gzip

We begin with one file. Create a file named `notes.txt` in your project directory, with any text in it. Then compress it into `notes.txt.gz` with this program:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val compressNotes: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("notes.txt")
    .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName("notes.txt.gz"))
```

`ZStream.fromFileName` reads the file in chunks. `GzipCompressor.compress` turns those chunks into compressed chunks, and `ZSink.fromFileName` writes them to the new file. Nothing is read until the program runs the pipeline with `run`.

### Step 3: Decompress the File

To decompress the file again, swap the compressor for a decompressor:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val decompressNotes: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("notes.txt.gz")
    .via(GzipDecompressor.decompress)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName("notes-copy.txt"))
```

The copy `notes-copy.txt` is identical to `notes.txt`. Gzip is a single-file format, so it does not record the file name. That is why the output name is chosen here.

### Step 4: Archive Several Files into a ZIP

A ZIP archive holds many entries, and each entry has a name and content. An entry is a pair of an `ArchiveEntry` and a stream of bytes. Build one entry per file, and let `ZipArchiver` write them:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

def fileEntry(path: String): (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any], ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte]) =
  (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any](path), ZStream.fromFileName(path))

val archiveNotes: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Long] =
  ZStream
    .fromIterable(Seq("notes.txt", "notes-copy.txt"))
    .map(fileEntry)
    .via(ZipArchiver().archive)
    .run(ZSink.fromFileName("bundle.zip"))
```

The entries do not need their size, so `ArchiveEntry[Option, Any](path)` is enough. `ZipArchiver` deflates each entry by default.

### Step 5: List the Archive

To check what is inside `bundle.zip`, read its entries back with `ZipUnarchiver`. The `list` method fills in the size of each entry:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

val listBundle: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Chunk[String]] =
  ZStream
    .fromFileName("bundle.zip")
    .via(ZipUnarchiver().list)
    .map(entry => s"${entry.name}: ${entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L)} bytes")
    .runCollect
```

When you need the content of each entry, use `unarchive` instead. Then read each entry's content before the next entry is emitted. The [Read Archives Safely](./how-to-read-archives-safely.md) guide explains why.

### Step 6: Put It All Together

Here is the complete program. It compresses `notes.txt`, bundles the files, and lists the archive:

```scala
import zio._
import zio.compress._
import zio.stream._

object CompressAndArchive extends ZIOAppDefault {

  private def fileEntry(path: String): (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any], ZStream[Any, Throwable, Byte]) =
    (ArchiveEntry[Option, Any](path), ZStream.fromFileName(path))

  override def run: ZIO[Any, Throwable, Unit] =
    for {
      _ <- ZStream
             .fromFileName("notes.txt")
             .via(GzipCompressor.compress)
             .run(ZSink.fromFileName("notes.txt.gz"))
      _ <- ZStream
             .fromIterable(Seq("notes.txt", "notes.txt.gz"))
             .map(fileEntry)
             .via(ZipArchiver().archive)
             .run(ZSink.fromFileName("bundle.zip"))
      entries <- ZStream
                   .fromFileName("bundle.zip")
                   .via(ZipUnarchiver().list)
                   .map(entry => s"${entry.name}: ${entry.uncompressedSize.getOrElse(-1L)} bytes")
                   .runCollect
      _ <- ZIO.foreachDiscard(entries)(line => Console.printLine(line))
    } yield ()
}
```

Run the program with `sbt run`. It prints one line per entry in `bundle.zip`.

### Where to Go Next

You now know how to compress a stream, decompress it, and archive several entries. The [Create and Read Archives](./how-to-create-and-read-archives.md) guide covers Tar archives, and the [Compress and Decompress](./how-to-compress-and-decompress.md) guide shows how to swap codecs without changing the rest of the program. For every option of every module, see the reference pages in the sidebar.

## Introduction to ZIO Telemetry

[ZIO telemetry](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry) is purely-functional and type-safe. It provides clients for
[OpenTracing](https://opentracing.io/), [OpenCensus](https://opencensus.io/) and [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/).

[![Production Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project%20Stage-Production%20Ready-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/zio/zio/wiki/Project-Stages) ![CI Badge](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/workflows/CI/badge.svg) [![Sonatype Releases](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/dev.zio/zio-opentracing_2.13.svg?label=Sonatype%20Release)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/dev.zio/zio-opentracing_2.13) [![Sonatype Snapshots](https://img.shields.io/maven-metadata/v?metadataUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fcentral.sonatype.com%2Frepository%2Fmaven-snapshots%2Fdev%2Fzio%2Fzio-opentracing_2.13%2Fmaven-metadata.xml&label=Sonatype%20Snapshot)](https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/dev/zio/zio-opentracing_2.13/) [![javadoc](https://javadoc.io/badge2/dev.zio/zio-opentracing_2.13/javadoc.svg)](https://javadoc.io/doc/dev.zio/zio-opentracing_2.13) [![ZIO Telemetry](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/zio/zio-telemetry?style=social)](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry)

ZIO Telemetry consists of the following projects:

- [OpenTracing](opentracing.md)
- [OpenCensus](opencensus.md)
- [OpenTelemetry](opentelemetry.md)

### Introduction

In monolithic architecture, everything is in one place, and we know when a request starts and then how it goes through 
the components and when it finishes. We can obviously see what is happening with our request and where is it going. 
But, in distributed systems like microservice architecture, we cannot find out the story of a request through various 
services easily. This is where distributed tracing comes into play.

ZIO Telemetry is a purely functional client which helps up propagate context between services in a distributed environment.

### Installation

In order to use this library, we need to add the following line in our `build.sbt` file if we want to use [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) client:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-opentelemetry" % "3.1.21"
```

If you're using [ZIO Logging](https://github.com/zio/zio-logging) you can combine OpenTelemetry with ZIO Logging using:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-opentelemetry-zio-logging" % "3.1.21"
```

For using [OpenTracing](https://opentracing.io/) client we should add the following line in our `build.sbt` file:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-opentracing" % "3.1.21"
```

And for using [OpenCensus](https://opencensus.io/) client we should add the following line in our `build.sbt` file:

```scala
libraryDependencies += "dev.zio" %% "zio-opencensus" % "3.1.21"
```

### Examples

You can find examples with full source code and instructions of how to run by following the links:
- [OpenTelemetry Example](opentelemetry-example.md)
- [OpenTelemetry Instrumentation Example](opentelemetry-instrumentation-example.md)
- [OpenTelemetry ZIO Logging Example](opentelemetry-zio-logging.md)
- [OpenTracing Example](opentracing-example.md)

### Articles

- [Trace your microservices with ZIO](https://kadek-marek.medium.com/trace-your-microservices-with-zio-telemetry-5f88d69cb26b) by Marek Kadek (September 2021)

## OpenCensus

OpenCensus is a stats collection and distributed tracing framework. Well known implementations are [Jaeger](https://www.jaegertracing.io)
and [Zipkin](https://www.zipkin.io).

### Installation

First, add the following dependency to your build.sbt:
```
"dev.zio" %% "zio-opencensus" % "3.1.21"
```

### Usage

To use ZIO Telemetry, you will need a `Tracing` service in your environment. You also need to provide a `tracer` implementation:

```scala
import zio.telemetry.opencensus.Tracing
import zio.telemetry.opencensus.implicits._
import zio._
import io.opencensus.trace.Status

val tracerLayer = ZLayer.succeed(io.opencensus.trace.Tracing.getTracer)

val errorMapper = ErrorMapper[Throwable] { case _ => Status.UNKNOWN }

val app =
  ZIO.serviceWithZIO[Tracing] { tracing =>
    import tracing.aspects._

    (for {
      _       <- tracing.putAttributes(Map("foo" -> "bar"))
      message <- Console.readline
    } yield message) @@ root("/app")
  }.provide(Tracing.live, tracerLayer)
```

After importing `import tracing.aspects._`, additional `ZIOAspect` combinators
on `ZIO`s are available to support starting child spans and adding attributes.

```scala
ZIO.serviceWithZIO[Tracing] { tracing =>
  import tracing.aspects._
  
  // start a new root span and set some attributes
  val zio1 = ZIO.unit @@ root("root span", attributes = ("foo", "bar))
  // start a child of the current span
  val zio2 = ZIO.unit @@ span("child span", attributes = Map.empty)
}
```

To propagate contexts across process boundaries, extraction and injection can be
used. The current span context is injected into a carrier, which is passed
through some side channel to the next process. There it is injected back and a
child span of it is started.

Due to the use of the (mutable) OpenCensus carrier APIs, injection and extraction
are not referentially transparent.

```scala
ZIO.serviceWithZIO[Tracing] { tracing =>
  import tracing.aspects._
  
  val textFormat                           = Tracing.getPropagationComponent().getB3Format()
  val carrier: mutable.Map[String, String] = mutable.Map().empty

  val getter: TextFormat.Getter[mutable.Map[String, String]] = new TextFormat.Getter[mutable.Map[String, String]] {
    override def keys(carrier: mutable.Map[String, String]): lang.Iterable[String] =
      carrier.keys.asJava

    override def get(carrier: mutable.Map[String, String], key: String): String =
      carrier.get(key).orNull
  }

  val setter: TextFormat.Setter[mutable.Map[String, String]] = new TextFormat.Setter[mutable.Map[String, String]] {
    override def put(carrier: mutable.Map[String, String], key: String, value: String): Unit =
      carrier.update(key, value)
  }
  
  val zio1 = tracing.inject(textFormat, carrier, setter) @@ 
    root("root span", attributes = Map.empty)
  
  val zio2 = ZIO.unit @@ 
    span("child span", attributes = Map(("foo", "bar"))) @@ 
    fromRootSpan(textFormat, carrier, getter, "foo", attributes = Map.empty)
}
```

## OpenTelemetry Example

You can find the source code [here](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/tree/series/2.x/opentelemetry-example).

For an explanation in more detail, check the [OpenTracing Example](opentracing-example.md).

We're going to show an example of how to pass contextual information using [Baggage](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/baggage/) and collect traces, metrics, and logs.

## Run

### Print OTEL signals to console

By default the example code uses [OTLP Logging Exporters](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/tree/main/exporters/logging-otlp) to print all signals to stdout in OTLP JSON encoding. This means that you can run the application immediately and observe the results.

For this, you need to run proxy and backend parts of application in different terminals via sbt.

Run proxy:
```bash
sbt "opentelemetryExample/runMain zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.example.ProxyApp"
```
Run backend:
```bash
sbt "opentelemetryExample/runMain zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.example.BackendApp"
```
Now perform the following request to see the results immediately:
```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/statuses
```

### Publish OTEL signals to other observability platforms

In case you want to try different observability platforms such as [Jaeger](https://www.jaegertracing.io/), [Fluentbit](https://fluentbit.io/), [Seq](https://datalust.co/seq), [DataDog](https://www.datadoghq.com/), [Honeycomb](https://www.honeycomb.io/) or others, please change the [OtelSdk.scala](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/blob/series/2.x/opentelemetry-example/src/main/scala/zio/telemetry/opentelemetry/example/otel/OtelSdk.scala) file by choosing from the available tracer, meter, and logger providers or by implementing your own. 

### Publish OTEL signals to Jaeger and Seq

We chose [Jaeger](https://www.jaegertracing.io/) for distributed traces and [Seq](https://datalust.co/seq) to store logs to demonstrate how the library works with available open-source observability platforms.

Start Jaeger by running the following command:
```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -d \
  -e COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true \
  -p 4317:4317 \
  -p 16686:16686 \
  jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.47
```

To run Seq, you also need to specify an admin password (user is `admin`):
```bash
PH=$(echo 'admin123' | docker run --rm -i datalust/seq config hash)

docker run \
  -d \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y \
  -e SEQ_FIRSTRUN_ADMINPASSWORDHASH="$PH" \
  -p 80:80 \
  -p 5341:5341 \
  datalust/seq
```

You must also switch the Tracing and Logging providers to Jaeger and Seq. For this, you need to swap the `stdout` providers we use by default in [OtelSdk.scala](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/blob/series/2.x/opentelemetry-example/src/main/scala/zio/telemetry/opentelemetry/example/otel/OtelSdk.scala#L10) to [TracerProvider.jaeger](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/blob/series/2.x/opentelemetry-example/src/main/scala/zio/telemetry/opentelemetry/example/otel/TracerProvider.scala#L37) and [LoggerProvider.seq](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/blob/series/2.x/opentelemetry-example/src/main/scala/zio/telemetry/opentelemetry/example/otel/LoggerProvider.scala#L36)

Run the application and fire a curl request as shown above. Head over to [Jaeger UI](http://localhost:16686/) and [Seq UI](http://localhost:80/) to see the result.

## OpenTelemetry Automatic Instrumentation Example

You can find the source code [here](https://github.com/zio/zio-telemetry/tree/series/2.x/opentelemetry-instrumentation-example).

Firstly, we need to start the observability backends ([Jaeger](https://www.jaegertracing.io/) and [Seq](https://datalust.co/seq))

Start Jaeger by running the following command:
```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -d \
  -e COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true \
  -p 14250:14250 \
  -p 16686:16686 \
  -p 4317:4317 \
  jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.47
 ```

To run Seq, you also need to specify an admin password (user is `admin`):
```bash
PH=$(echo 'admin123' | docker run --rm -i datalust/seq config hash)

docker run \
  -d \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y \
  -e SEQ_FIRSTRUN_ADMINPASSWORDHASH="$PH" \
  -p 80:80 \
  -p 5341:5341 \
  datalust/seq
```

After this, we can kick off our application to generate some metrics.

For this, we have to download OpenTelemetry JVM agent JAR:
```bash
OTEL_AGENT_PATH=$(cs fetch --classpath "io.opentelemetry.javaagent:opentelemetry-javaagent:latest.release")
 ```

Then start the server application
```bash
sbt -J-javaagent:$OTEL_AGENT_PATH \
    -J-Dotel.service.name=example-server \
    -J-Dotel.traces.sampler=always_on \
    -J-Dotel.traces.exporter=otlp \
    -J-Dotel.logs.exporter=otlp \
    -J-Dotel.exporter.otlp.logs.protocol="http/protobuf" \
    -J-Dotel.exporter.otlp.logs.endpoint="http://localhost:5341/ingest/otlp/v1/logs" \
    -J-Dotel.metrics.exporter=none \
    "opentelemetryInstrumentationExample/runMain zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.instrumentation.example.ServerApp"
 ```

and the client application which will send one request to the server application
```bash
sbt -J-javaagent:$OTEL_AGENT_PATH \
    -J-Dotel.service.name=example-client \
    -J-Dotel.traces.sampler=always_on \
    -J-Dotel.traces.exporter=otlp \
    -J-Dotel.metrics.exporter=none \
    "opentelemetryInstrumentationExample/runMain zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.instrumentation.example.ClientApp"
 ```

Head over to [Jaeger UI](http://localhost:16686/) and [Seq UI](http://localhost:80/) to see the result.

## OpenTelemetry ZIO Logging

`zio-opentelemetry` logging facilities are implemented around OpenTelemetry Logging.

In order to use `zio-opentelemetry` feature with `zio-logging` you should use `zio-opentelemetry-zio-logging` module.

`OpenTelemetry ZIO Logging` contains utilities for combining ZIO Opentelemetry with ZIO Logging

### Installation

```scala
"dev.zio" %% "zio-opentelemetry-zio-logging" % "3.1.21"
```

### Features

#### Log formats

This library implements [Log Format](https://zio.dev/zio-logging/formatting-log-records) for span information (`spanId` and `traceId`). 
To use them you need a `LogFormats` service in the environment. For this, use the `ZioLogging.logFormats` layer which in turn required a suitable `ContextStorage` implementation.

```scala
//> using scala "3.4.2"
//> using dep dev.zio::zio:2.1.7
//> using dep dev.zio::zio-opentelemetry:3.0.0-RC24
//> using dep dev.zio::zio-opentelemetry-zio-logging:3.0.0-RC24
//> using dep io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-sdk:1.40.0
//> using dep io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-sdk-trace:1.40.0
//> using dep io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-logging-otlp:1.40.0
//> using dep io.opentelemetry.semconv:opentelemetry-semconv:1.22.0-alpha

import io.opentelemetry.exporter.logging.otlp.OtlpJsonLoggingSpanExporter
import io.opentelemetry.exporter.logging.otlp.OtlpJsonLoggingLogRecordExporter
import io.opentelemetry.api.common.Attributes
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.trace.SdkTracerProvider
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.trace.`export`.SimpleSpanProcessor
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.logs.SdkLoggerProvider
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.logs.`export`.SimpleLogRecordProcessor
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.resources.Resource
import io.opentelemetry.semconv.ServiceAttributes
import io.opentelemetry.sdk.OpenTelemetrySdk
import io.opentelemetry.api
import zio.*
import zio.logging.console
import zio.logging.LogFormat._
import zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.tracing.Tracing
import zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.OpenTelemetry
import zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.context.ContextStorage
import zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.zio.logging.LogFormats
import zio.telemetry.opentelemetry.zio.logging.ZioLogging

object ZioLoggingApp extends ZIOAppDefault {

  val instrumentationScopeName = "dev.zio.LoggingApp"
  val resourceName             = "logging-app"

  // Prints to stdout in OTLP Json format
  val stdoutLoggerProvider: RIO[Scope, SdkLoggerProvider] =
    for {
      logRecordExporter  <- ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(ZIO.succeed(OtlpJsonLoggingLogRecordExporter.create()))
      logRecordProcessor <- ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(ZIO.succeed(SimpleLogRecordProcessor.create(logRecordExporter)))
      loggerProvider     <-
        ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(
          ZIO.succeed(
            SdkLoggerProvider
              .builder()
              .setResource(Resource.create(Attributes.of(ServiceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME, resourceName)))
              .addLogRecordProcessor(logRecordProcessor)
              .build()
          )
        )
    } yield loggerProvider

  // Prints to stdout in OTLP Json format
  val stdoutTracerProvider: RIO[Scope, SdkTracerProvider] =
    for {
      spanExporter   <- ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(ZIO.succeed(OtlpJsonLoggingSpanExporter.create()))
      spanProcessor  <- ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(ZIO.succeed(SimpleSpanProcessor.create(spanExporter)))
      tracerProvider <-
        ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(
          ZIO.succeed(
            SdkTracerProvider
              .builder()
              .setResource(Resource.create(Attributes.of(ServiceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME, resourceName)))
              .addSpanProcessor(spanProcessor)
              .build()
          )
        )
    } yield tracerProvider

  val otelSdkLayer: TaskLayer[api.OpenTelemetry] =
    OpenTelemetry.custom(
      for {
        tracerProvider <- stdoutTracerProvider
        loggerProvider <- stdoutLoggerProvider
        sdk            <- ZIO.fromAutoCloseable(
                            ZIO.succeed(
                              OpenTelemetrySdk
                                .builder()
                                .setTracerProvider(tracerProvider)
                                .setLoggerProvider(loggerProvider)
                                .build()
                            )
                          )
      } yield sdk
    )

  // Setup zio-logging with spanId and traceId labels
  val loggingLayer: URLayer[LogFormats, Unit] = ZLayer {
    for {
      logFormats     <- ZIO.service[LogFormats]
      format          =
        timestamp.fixed(32) |-|
          level |-|
          label("message", quoted(line)) |-|
          logFormats.spanIdLabel |-|
          logFormats.traceIdLabel
      myConsoleLogger = console(format.highlight)
    } yield Runtime.removeDefaultLoggers >>> myConsoleLogger
  }.flatten

  override def run =
    ZIO
      .serviceWithZIO[Tracing] { tracing =>
        val logic = for {
          // Read user input
          message <- Console.readLine
          // Print span and trace ids along with message
          _       <- ZIO.logInfo(s"User message: $message")
        } yield ()

        // All log messages produced by `logic` will be correlated with a "root_span" automatically
        logic @@ tracing.aspects.root("root_span")
      }
      .provide(
        otelSdkLayer,
        OpenTelemetry.logging(instrumentationScopeName),
        OpenTelemetry.tracing(instrumentationScopeName),
        OpenTelemetry.contextZIO,
        ZioLogging.logFormats,
        loggingLayer
      )

}
```
